ce9bb767cc.title: Inside Google’s Failure to Make Google Maps Work for Palestinians
ce9bb767cc.summary: On the road that connects the villages to the north of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank, there is always a watch tower and a gate, often flanked by Israeli soldiers with machine guns around their necks. None of these things are visible on Google Maps. Where drivers see a checkpoint , a barrier and soldiers searching cars, the world’s most popular navigation app renders a clear blue line indicating the coast is clear. This story was produced in partnership with the Palestine Reporting Lab , Arab Reporters for Investigative Journalism (ARIJ), Lighthouse Reports and Evident . Routes and maps are not just a matter of journey times or congestion for the nearly 3.5 million Palestinians in the West Bank. Drivers there are forced to navigate a growing and arbitrary system of more than 900 movement obstacles , like checkpoints, which can be policed with lethal force. For Palestinians, these roads can be a matter of life or death. Google Maps could help them make safer choices. It has failed for years to do so. Google has the ability to alert checkpoints, a feature that it added to Maps in some locations around the world during the Covid crisis. It is aware of the problems experienced by Palestinian drivers in the West Bank. In fact, a former Google product manager spent six years trying to get Maps to serve Palestinians in the same way it serves the rest of the world. Interviews with more than a dozen former and current Google employees reveal for the first time the inner tensions at the heart of the Google Maps project. Multiple former employees described how the company abandoned the effort and settled on a map that fails, and even harms, Palestinians. As we revealed last month, Palestinians in the West Bank have bootstrapped makeshift navigation solutions such as the popular Road Conditions Telegram channel to help them go about their lives more safely – achieving what Google will not. Rubén Lozano joined Google Maps as a product manager in 2019. He devoted his days to keeping track of hyperlocal driving restrictions, making sure that what appeared on the map matched what appeared on the ground. He fielded emails from Barcelona city officials about small shifts in their emission zones and flew to Australia to document one city’s toll prices. Whatever he missed, drivers were sure to alert in feedback forums. c97da7a39e.title: Why Palestine was absent and Miss Israel booed at Miss Universe 2026
c97da7a39e.summary: Israel's representative drew a mixed reaction during the Miss Universe 2026 pageant in Puerto Rico on Saturday. Danielle Yablonka, 25, wore an outfit featuring images of occupied East Jerusalem's Old City and a message of peace, during the national costume segment of the competition. Sections of the audience jeered as she took to the stage in San Juan, although some people applauded and cheered. Nadeen Ayoub on representing Palestine at Miss Universe: 'We should never be silenced' The Israeli contestant continued her walk, smiling as she displayed a gold bodysuit, matching boots and an elaborate crown, along with a cape depicting Jerusalem , olive trees and Jaffa oranges. The Old City is in East Jerusalem and is considered, by the UN and most of the international community, to be part of Israeli-occupied Palestinian territory. Yablonka's costume, designed by Jerusalem-born Jacob Meir, also featured versions of the word “peace” in Hebrew, Arabic and English, as well as the phrase “Jerusalem, City of Peace”. “I wanted this costume to tell the story of Israel beyond the headlines,” Yablonka told The Times of Israel. Her appearance sparked debate online, with some questioning the use of Jerusalem's imagery amid the continuing war in Gaza and tension between Israelis and Palestinians. Nadeen Ayoub , who made history last year as the first Palestinian woman to take part in Miss Universe, questioned the meaning of Jerusalem being featured on Miss Israel's costume at a pageant where Palestine had no representative this year. “Last year, I wore Jerusalem on my back as the first Palestinian woman to compete at Miss Universe. This year, Jerusalem appeared on Miss Israel's costume while Palestine had no delegate on that stage,” she told The National . “That's what's at stake when we're absent. The world still sees images of Jerusalem, but it doesn't hear from a Palestinian woman about what they mean to us.” Jerusalem remains one of the most contentious issues between Palestinians and Israelis. Since 1967, Israel has occupied East Jerusalem, claiming it, along with West Jerusalem, as its capital. Meanwhile, Palestinians seek East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state. Ayoub, who reached the top 30 at Miss Universe 2025 in Thailand, had planned to help select a Palestinian representative for this year's competition. In August, she and the Miss Palestine Organisation announced plans for a national pageant , open to Palestinian women living in Palestine…

a01867392a.title: OpenAI Science Head Calls for Limits to AI Development
a01867392a.summary: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki is calling for artificial intelligence companies to create “shared norms” for evaluating their AI models. Beyond that, he is also proposing limits on model development until researchers can figure better ways to track their behavior, according to a company blog post Sunday (Nov. 22). “I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models and red-team safety cases for them by the time they are first used, including shared transparency standards,” Pachocki wrote. “I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone.” He defined perplexity as a measure of “how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions.” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman offered his support to Pachoki’s plan in a post on X, calling it the “most important thing” the company has published “in a while.” “We are providing a lot of transparency into our pretraining progress and hope we can agree as a field to common limits,” Altman wrote. “I think that would be very wise and help ensure safety and control.” Pachoki’s proposal was published the same day that the National Governors Association (NGA) unveiled a set of principles aimed at helping states develop a “shared national approach” to AI regulations as the new Congress prepares to take office in the new year. “Governors from across the country agree that AI poses both opportunities and risks,” Maryland Gov. Wes Moore, who chairs the NGA, said in a news release. “We agree that humans must stay in control , and we must protect our people — especially workers, consumers and our kids. Governors will continue to focus both on creating jobs and making sure that workers have a voice in deployment of new technology.” Meanwhile, new proposed House legislation would establish a federal board to investigate major cyberattacks, artificial intelligence incidents and technological failures . “The proposal comes after a midterm campaign in which polling showed widespread concern over AI safety,” PYMNTS wrote last week. “In the weeks before Democrats take control of Congress in January, lawmakers from both parties are pressing for a federal role in investigating critical system failures and addressing the risks posed by AI agents that can act on their own.”…

The IPO does not make those costs disappear; it broadens the group of people and institutions carrying them. Until now, much of the cost of building frontier AI has been borne by venture capitalists, sovereign investors and the large technology companies. Public market investors are now being asked to take on a share of that burden. A lot now rides on how Anthropic’s shares trade — if they do well, this will encourage more late-stage AI companies to go public. f94370bf32.summary: Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) made stock market history on Nov. 19, completing the largest initial public offering (IPO) ever. The artificial intelligence (AI) developer behind Claude raised $81 billion , surpassing the roughly $75 billion raised by Elon Musk's Space Exploration Technologies earlier this year. The blockbuster debut illustrates Wall Street's appetite for premier AI stocks. However, Anthropic's valuation raises an important question: Is the frontier lab a better investment than Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), the semiconductor giant powering much of the AI revolution? Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Although Anthropic's growth is impressive, Nvidia offers a more attractive combination of profitability, valuation, and shareholder returns. Let's dig into why. Anthropic is experiencing unprecedented commercial momentum as enterprises integrate Claude models into their operations. The company's revenue increased from $386 million in 2024 to $4.6 billion in 2025, representing growth of roughly 1,090%. During the first nine months of 2026, revenue reached $33.2 billion, demonstrating the rapid acceleration in demand for its AI products. Perhaps even more impressive, Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of the end of October. Moreover, the number of customers generating at least $100,000 in trailing annual revenue increased from more than 950 in September 2025 to more than 11,900 in September 2026. With that said, Anthropic's valuation already reflects enormous expectations. As of this writing (Nov. 20), Anthropic boasts a market capitalization of roughly $1.2 trillion. This implies the company trades at roughly 14.8 times its $81 billion annualized revenue run rate. To be clear, this is different from a conventional price-to-sales (P/S) ratio since the run rate annualizes recent activity rather than measuring revenue actually generated over 12 months. More importantly, Anthropic is unprofitable. The company reported an operating loss of roughly $1.3 billion during the first nine months of 2026. In addition, its underlying operations incur significant expenses for training and operating AI models. d93434e975.title: Anthropic Boss Dario Amodei's Alleged Solution for Simulating a Fulfilling Life for People Who Lose Their Jobs to AI
d93434e975.summary: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei reportedly once suggested that video games could be the solution to political strife caused by AI-fueled joblessness. In a profile of Anthropic’s Dario and Daniela Amodei from the Wall Street Journal , it is reported that when Dario Amodei worked at OpenAI from 2016 to 2020, he allegedly suggested video games could pacify the masses after AI took their jobs. Here’s the relevant section of the profile: The anecdote suggests a foresight from Dario Amodei about the potential of AI to cause mass layoffs, but also a rather dystopian solution that would see jobless people content to live out their lives playing video games rather than kick up a stink about losing their livelihoods. While this section of the WSJ profile mentioned Amodei’s alleged thoughts on this issue from some time ago (potentially a decade ago), and he may have changed his mind since then, it’s interesting to consider his mindset in the context of growing concern around mass layoffs as companies turn to AI to replace human workers to save money and, they claim, boost productivity. Survey data from Pew Research Center published in September showed how ordinary people around the world are worried about the economic impact of AI. In 34 of 37 countries Pew Research Center surveyed earlier this year , people tend to believe AI will lead to fewer jobs rather than more jobs. And people are getting more worried about this over time. In the U.S., the share of people who believe AI will result in job loss over the next 20 years increased seven percentage points in two years. The profile also has a delicious timing, coming as it does around the launch of GTA 6 , a game that you’d imagine Dario Amodei might have considered to be a video game "immersive enough" to pacify the jobless masses long term. Reaction online to the profile is, predictably, a mix of outrage and mockery, with some posting The Matrix and Ready Player One memes in response. "Unless we’d get paid for playing video games, I don’t see how that would work. Boredom isn’t the problem with joblessness," one person said. “How do people buy games if they don't have a job that pays them?” another wondered. The answer from people who are convinced of our AI-powered future to that common retort is, as Elon Musk is fond of saying, abundance for all. 935ad44832.summary: The new model beats its predecessor on coding and cost but slips on chat, debuting behind Anthropic and Google DeepMind Sat 21 Nov 2026 · 12:26 EST · 3 min read OpenAI ’s newest flagship model has its first public report card, and the grade is respectable but not top of the class. GPT-6.2 Astra debuted at sixth place on the Agent Arena Index with a score of 1,291. The ranking comes from Arena.ai, which launched the index just one day after OpenAI released the model. The result is a model that got noticeably better at writing code and noticeably worse at making conversation. OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra on November 17, 2026. The company positions it as an advanced model built for complex professional and scientific work. It arrived alongside a sibling, GPT-6.2 Sol, which is the more efficient option of the pair. Both models are aimed at OpenAI’s main products: ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the OpenAI API. Pricing is a big part of the pitch. Input and output tokens for GPT-6.2 Astra cost 20% less than they did for GPT-6 Astra, its predecessor. Cached input gets a steeper cut, with a 60% discount. Cached input refers to content the model has already processed and can reuse, like a long instruction set sent with every request. OpenAI has also said the model set new benchmark highs on tests including Agents’ Last Exam and Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1. The company reported reaching those scores at lower costs per task than its previous model managed. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. The Agent Arena Index aggregates data from more than 2.9 million real user sessions, measuring how models behave when people actually put them to work. The index tracks four signals. The first is task completion, which asks whether the agent finished the job. The second is user satisfaction, measured by comparing how often users praise a model against how often they complain about it. The third is steerability, meaning how well the model follows direction when a user tries to redirect it. The fourth is bash reliability. Bash is the command-line shell developers use to run programs and manage files, so this measures whether an agent can operate a terminal without breaking things. f3e76cdbe5.summary: للاطلاع على أسعار الذهب أولا بأول اضغط هنا لزيارة موقع رؤيا أسعار الذهب. انْتَعَشَتْ أَسْعَارُ الذَّهَبِ، اليَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنَ، مُعَوِّضَةً جُزْءاً مِنْ أَكْبَرِ خَسَارَةٍ رِهَانَاتِهَا عَلَى رَفْعِ مَجْلِسِ الِاحْتِيَاطِيِّ الفِيدْرَالِيِّ الأَمِيرْكِيِّ أَسْعَارَ الفَائِدَةِ فِي شَهْرِ كَانُونَ الأَوَّلِ/دِيسَمْبَر المُقْبِلِ. وَارْتَفَعَ سِعْرُ المَعْدِنِ النَّفِيسِ بِمَا يَصِلُ إِلَى 2.8% لِيَبْلُغَ نَحْوَ 3,637 دُولَاراً لِلْأُونْصَةِ، بَعْدَمَا تَرَاجَعَ بِنِسْبَةِ 9% الأُسْبُوعَ المَاضِي إِلَى أَدْنَى مُسْتَوًى لَهُ مُنْذُ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ عَامٍ؛ فِيمَا انْخَفَضَ مُؤَشِّرُ القُوَّةِ النِّسْبِيَّةِ لِلذَّهَبِ خِلَالَ 14 يَوْماً إِلَى أَقَلَّ مِنْ 30 نُقْطَةً، مَا يُشِيرُ إِلَى احْتِمَالِ وُصُولِ المَعْدِنِ إِلَى مَرْحَلَةِ التَّشَبُّعِ البَيْعِيِّ. الرَّئِيسِيَّ لِتِجَارَةِ الذَّهَبِ بِالتَّجْزِئَةِ فِي البِلَادِ بِالمُتَسَوِّقِينَ الرَّاغِبِينَ فِي شِرَاءِ المَجُوهَرَاتِ؛ حَيْثُ أَوْضَحَ البَاحِثُ فِي أَكَادِيمِيَّةِ سُوقِ الذَّهَبِ بِجَنُوبِ 5dd653293f.title: Blacklisted Chinese universities procured Nvidia chips, records show
5dd653293f.summary: At least six Chinese universities blacklisted by the US government have reported purchasing restricted Nvidia computer chips in recent years, a CNN review of business records found – highlighting US difficulties in controlling access to the in-demand technology. Two of those universities known for their ties to the Chinese military establishment reported buying the high-powered chips just in the last few months. The number of universities involved and full scope of their Nvidia purchases have not been previously reported. The purchases, made through obscure sellers in China, were for relatively small amounts of older chips, not the industrial, cutting-edge computing technology that researchers fear could enable China to overtake the US in the artificial intelligence race. Still, they show how widely available restricted Nvidia chips remain inside China, and how difficult it is for the US to block the sale of the chips even to some of the most high-risk entities – a particularly sensitive concern following allegations linking Nvidia’s CEO to a potential Chinese intelligence asset. “Once these chips are in China, it’s very hard for anyone to be able to stop their sale,” said Kate Koren, a former US export control official who now serves as a research director at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. “We know it happens, and it’s very difficult to stop.” The issue is likely to be a major talking point in this week’s high-stakes meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping as the White House moves to close loopholes that have allowed sensitive, AI-powering computer chips into China. Concerns spiked over Chinese access to the technology as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned last week following the revelation he had a romantic relationship with a woman whose former company is suspected of helping smuggle chips into the country. f983d506db.title: Cognition, 75 milyar dolar değerleme üzerinden yeni yatırım için görüşmeler yürütüyor
f983d506db.summary: Yapay zeka destekli yazılım geliştirme platformu Cognition , yeni bir yatırım turu için görüşmeler yapıyor. Reuters'in haberine göre şirket, 75 milyar dolar değerleme üzerinden 2 milyar dolar veya daha fazla yatırım almayı planlıyor. Görüşmelerin sürdüğü, yatırımın miktarının ve koşullarının değişebileceği belirtiliyor. Cognition , henüz iki ay önce 48 milyar dolar değerleme üzerinden 2 milyar dolarlık yatırım almıştı . Andreessen Horowitz ve Accel'in öncülük ettiği yatırım turuna şirketin mevcut yatırımcıları Founders Fund, General Catalyst ve Avenir de katılmıştı. Şirket, 2026 yılı boyunca şimdiye kadar 3 milyar doların üzerinde yatırım aldı. Cognition, yazılım geliştirme süreçlerindeki işleri kendi başına yerine getirebilen yapay zeka araçları geliştiriyor. Şirketin Devin adlı ürünü kod yazabiliyor, yazdığı kodları test edebiliyor ve yazılımları kullanıma hazır hale getirebiliyor. Bu alanda SpaceX'in 60 milyar dolara satın aldığı Cursor ile rekabet ediyor. Citigroup ve Nvidia gibi şirketleri müşterileri arasında sayan Cognition, eylül ayında yıllıklandırılmış gelirinin 1 milyar dolara ulaşmasını beklediğini açıklamıştı. Şirketin gelirinin, dört ay öncesine göre yaklaşık iki katına çıktığı belirtilmişti. Yeni yatırım turunun tamamlanması halinde Cognition, 2026 yılında üçüncü kez yatırım almış olacak. Ancak 75 milyar dolarlık değerleme üzerinden yürütülen görüşmeler henüz sonuçlanmadı.

11544a4317.title: Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO'luğuna geri döndü
11544a4317.summary: Nvidia , kurucu ortağı Jensen Huang 'ın 23 Kasım'da yeniden CEO olarak göreve başladığını duyurdu . Yönetim kurulunun oy birliğiyle aldığı kararla Huang, şirket başkanlığına ve yönetim kurulu üyeliğine de döndü. Geçici CEO olarak görev yapan Colette Kress , CFO olarak devam edecek. Harvey C. Jones ise yönetim kurulu başkanlığını sürdürecek. Nvidia, Huang'ın istifasını 12 Kasım'da duyurmuştu . Şirketin ABD Menkul Kıymetler ve Borsa Komisyonu'na (SEC) yaptığı bildirime göre yönetim kurulu istifayı 11 Kasım'da kabul etti. Jones, 17 Kasım'daki finansal sonuçlar toplantısında Huang'ın şirketin davranış kuralları ve standartlarıyla bağdaşmayan kişisel davranışlarının ortaya çıkmasının ardından kendi isteğiyle görevlerinden ayrıldığını söyledi. Jones, aynı toplantıda yönetim kurulunun Huang'ı yeniden CEO olarak atamayı düşünmediğini de belirtti . Reuters'ın haberine göre istifa, Huang'ın evlilik dışı ilişkilerinin ortaya çıkmasının ardından geldi. Huang'ın ilişki yaşadığı kişilerden birinin Çin adına casusluk yaptığından ABD makamlarının şüphelendiği bildirildi. Pekin bu iddiayı reddetti. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ise Huang'ın göreve dönmesine destek verdi. Nvidia yönetim kurulu, Huang'la yaptığı görüşmelerin ardından açıklamalarını samimi bulduğunu ve şirketi yönetebileceğine kanaat getirdiğini bildirdi. 7c52448981.title: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
7c52448981.summary: July bug overwhelmed newer servers, prompting promises of stronger safeguards and faster recovery Some emails never reached their recipients during November's Microsoft 365 outage, the company has confirmed in a final report that also exposes gaps in its testing and recovery procedures. The post-incident report details how a Windows defect brought down Exchange Online and disrupted features across other Microsoft 365 services. For affected users, the cloud became someone else's unavailable computer. A preliminary report had already blamed a July code change, combined with a failover and reduced capacity. The final report confirms those findings and sets out Microsoft's plans to improve change auditing and recovery procedures, and add spare capacity. The defect affected Microsoft's gateway server configuration, not standard Windows deployments. The epic outage (named the "Microsoft long weekend" by some wags) kicked off on November 12 and wasn't fully resolved until November 14. Microsoft extended its delivery retry window to 48 hours, but some delayed messages destined for consumer mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days still expired, generating non-delivery reports. The company said all queued enterprise messages were eventually delivered, with none found permanently lost. The report is grim, particularly in how the failure ramped up as US users came online to find gateway servers toppling over. At the worst point, more than 80 percent of North American gateway servers were unresponsive. The problem proved elusive, and it took Microsoft some time to identify the change and deploy a fix. Microsoft has had a week to ponder what it did and did not do, and the report has some next steps to avoid a repeat of November's events. Some are obvious, and some are a little surprising. Working to reduce the blast radius of failures is an obvious one, and actions include partitioning and isolation to ensure failures can be contained before taking down traffic globally. Recovery procedures also need improvement, along with communication and capacity to ensure there is sufficient headroom. Microsoft's load tests used older, lower-core-count hardware, making them less likely to expose a defect that worsened on newer machines. The company now plans to test newer hardware with more realistic traffic and peak loads, and broaden its failover testing. Microsoft also plans to improve diagnostics and change auditing so engineers can identify troublesome Windows changes…

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is backing a proposal to put industrywide limits on developing increasingly powerful artificial intelligence models, warning that AI capabilities could advance faster than companies can safely monitor them. OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki outlined the proposal Sunday, November 22, urging rival developers to agree on thresholds they would not cross until stronger safety safeguards are established. The proposal centers on perplexity , a measurement of how accurately AI models predict the next piece of text. Lower scores generally indicate stronger predictive capabilities. Pachocki argues that improvements in this metric have accompanied major advances, including sophisticated cybersecurity abilities and mathematical problem-solving. OpenAI disclosed internal measurements showing GPT-3.5 had a log-perplexity score around 0.99, while newer models have moved below 0.8. Pachocki expects further potentially transformative capabilities around 0.68 to 0.70, although their exact nature remains unknown. Altman endorsed the proposal, describing Pachocki's essay as OpenAI's most important publication in some time. Pachocki warned that AI could begin substantially improving its own training methods as early as 2027, potentially accelerating development beyond existing safety capabilities. For investors in Nvidia (NVDA), Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ), Alphabet (GOOGL) and other AI-linked companies, coordinated restrictions could eventually influence the pace of frontier-model training and infrastructure spending. However, no binding industrywide agreement has been announced. The immediate question is whether competing AI developers can agree on common measurement standards and enforceable safeguards without surrendering their competitive advantages.

It must also change its behavior if an obstacle appears. Understanding the meaning of words and acting on them in the real world are entirely different challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to learn about the physical world, going beyond language. Physical AI, which perceives and moves through its surroundings, is emerging as a central focus of the next-generation technology race, moving beyond generative AI that writes and answers questions. But robots still have a long way to go before they can act like people. The biggest hurdle is their lack of experience accumulated in the real world. In an interview with The Asia Business Daily, Im Seonghun, a professor at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) Graduate School of Culture Technology and founder of Neural Dynamics, said, "While language models learn patterns in language and knowledge from vast amounts of text, robots need to learn what results follow from taking certain actions in particular situations." Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have advanced by learning from vast amounts of text accumulated on the internet. Robots, by contrast, cannot learn how to pick up an object just by reading. They need to experience the object's weight and friction, as well as changes in the environment as it moves. The technology driving this shift is the Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model. It surveys its surroundings through camera footage, understands a person's instructions, and then generates the robot's movements. This is a leading approach to robot foundation models trained for use across a range of tasks. a436e4c384.summary: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. Subscribe now Chinese researchers optimize Huawei chips with a kernel improvement benchmark: …AscendGYM will help China do its own form of RSI… Researchers with the Shenzhen Loop Area Institute, a Chinese research organization, have built and released AscendGYM, “a kernel optimization benchmark for Ascend NPUs”. The purpose of AscendGYM is to make it easier to use AI to develop custom kernels for Ascend chips from Huawei – especially important given the export controls that prevent Chinese organizations from acquiring frontier Western semiconductors and forcing them onto Huawei. What AscendGYM does and contains: The goal is for AscendGYM to be the best way to evaluate the efficacy of AI-designed kernels as well as design new ones. The software is meant to help researchers answer this question: “Given a correct kernel implementation, can the specific agent further improve its performance for a target workload within an acceptable budget while preserving correctness?,” they write. “AscendGYM evaluates performance across multiple deployment cases, the best achievable performance for specific shapes and scenarios, and the optimization cost required to obtain these gains. Together, these dimensions characterize cross-case applicability, shape specialization, and optimization efficiency.” The software includes the AscendForge evaluation environment, which provides unified interfaces for “compilation, correctness checking, performance measurement, and feedback”. How well can AI models optimize Ascend chips? In tests, the single best model is Opus 5, followed by GPT-5.6, followed by GLM-5.3. They test out models in Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode; Claude Code yields the best absolute scores, and GLM does well in it, while GPT does well in Codex. Opus 5 is more token hungry and GPT-5.6 more token efficient. Why this matters – ingredients for Chinese RSI: For AI systems to be able to build themselves, they need to be able to develop and improve the software that is used for their own training and inference. Software like AscendGYM will be an essential ingredient for allowing China to rapidly improve the efficiency of its own compute substrates. The software will also have a bearing on export controls, where it provides a route to improve the performance of Chinese chips and close the gap with Western alternatives. Read more: AscendGYM: A…

592d4094ad.title: Microsoft's Outlook outage came down to a perfect storm
592d4094ad.summary: Microsoft Outlook and other services went down for millions of people on November 12, 2026. The outage was so big that it dominated headlines even as flights were grounded in the United States due to FAA issues. Now, we have more details on what caused services to go down and why it took Microsoft so long to restore normal functionality. Microsoft shared a preliminary post-incident report on November 16, which can be found in the Admin center under MO1550821. Microsoft EVP of Copilot and Platform, Charles Lamanna, shared a summary of findings on X . The full incident report is now up as well. According to Microsoft, the outage was caused and extended by a months-old software defect that only surfaced under very specific conditions, increased traffic flowing through the affected infrastructure, and roughly 14% of server capacity being offline for unrelated reasons. Microsoft's planned maintenance, the shifting of Teams traffic to Exchange Online gateways, and peak traffic in North America combined to expose the latent defect. With limited capacity available, Microsoft service traffic was redistributed to healthy servers worldwide, which spread the effect of the problem. Recovery from the outage was extended because Microsoft had to identify the defect, which had sat unnoticed for months. Microsoft also needed to restart its affected servers before applying fixes and then restart them again to activate the update. It was essentially a perfect storm. Microsoft's systems are designed with multiple layers of resilience, but those factors aligned to trigger the dormant bug. A separate containment mechanism that should have prevented the outage from spreading also failed, allowing it to become a global disruption. The outage slowed down or halted work across several sectors. Notably, no email was lost due to the outage. All messages were queued and then delivered successfully. Microsoft's full incident report is an interesting read that breaks down how an outage like this can happen. It also includes a detailed timeline of each step in the process of finding the issue, identifying the cause, and fixing the root problems. Perhaps most important for everyday users is what Microsoft has learned from the incident. The company plans to fix traffic distribution to eliminate cascade failures in the future. Microsoft will also make failure zones smaller, partition network gateway capacity, and change how Teams traffic responds to failure. If Microsoft can complete its…

1622514ca5.title: CyberCube activates cyber catastrophe response after global Microsoft outage
1622514ca5.summary: CyberCube activated its Cyber Aggregation Event Response Service (CAERS) on November 13, 2026, following a widespread Microsoft outage that disrupted cloud-based business services across more than 75 countries. The incident began on November 12, when users lost access to Exchange Online mailboxes. Disruption subsequently extended to other Microsoft 365 applications dependent on Exchange, including some functionality within Teams and Copilot. CyberCube initiated its catastrophe response procedures to assess the potential insurance implications of the outage, focusing on business interruption exposure and the concentration of insured organisations dependent on Microsoft’s infrastructure. The company said it was preparing a Security Incident Report (SIR) for clients by the end of November 13, Eastern Time, with additional guidance to follow as the incident developed. Its CAERS service provides intelligence and analysis of major cyber events as they unfold, helping insurers and reinsurers evaluate accumulated exposures and potential financial losses. The duration of the Microsoft disruption has become a central consideration for insurers assessing potential business interruption claims. Third-party measurements indicated that Exchange Online traffic remained depressed for approximately 18 hours. Microsoft’s own incident timeline showed that the disruption had continued for more than 24 hours. These durations exceed the waiting periods commonly included in cyber insurance policies covering non-malicious technology outages. Contingent systems failure coverage, which can respond when an insured business suffers interruption because of an external technology provider, typically applies waiting periods of eight to 12 hours. William Altman, Director of Threat Intelligence Services at CyberCube, said the incident had already passed an important insurance threshold. This is a significant outage, and it has already lasted longer than the waiting periods in many cyber policies. We’re watching closely to see how long the disruption lasts, and we are advising clients to use our technology dependency mapping tools and portfolio risk modeling solutions to identify exposure and estimate potential losses. Exceeding a waiting period does not automatically establish an insured loss. 7ff5637ae3.title: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI use AI agents to build formally verified quantum algorithms
7ff5637ae3.summary: A new preprint pairs Gemini-based agents with the Lean 4 theorem prover and reports resource savings of over 290× on one quantum arithmetic task Mon 23 Nov 2026 · 12:03 EST · 3 min read Designing quantum algorithms has long been slow, painstaking work done by small groups of human specialists. Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI think a team of AI agents can share some of that load. In a preprint posted to arXiv, the two Google groups describe a multi-agent system that writes quantum programs and then proves mathematically that those programs are correct. The reported efficiency gains reach over 290× on one benchmark task. The paper is titled “Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI” and is listed as arXiv:2611.09822. It was first posted on November 6, 2026, and revised through mid-November. Lead authors include Sergey Shirobokov and Ben Jaderberg. Roughly 25 contributors from Google teams worked on it. The system has two main parts. The first is a set of large language model agents built on Google’s Gemini models. The second is Lean 4, a theorem prover that checks mathematical proofs line by line. Those circuits must satisfy formal specifications written in quantum Hoare logic. The method describes what must be true before a program runs and what must be true afterward. If the program cannot be proven to move from one state to the other, it fails. The output is more than working code. Each program ships with a machine-checked proof that it does what it claims. The system also tallies how expensive each program would be to run. It measures cost in two units: logical qubits and T gates. Logical qubits are the reliable, error-corrected qubits that future quantum machines will build from many noisy physical ones. T gates are a specific kind of operation that is notoriously costly to perform in error-corrected hardware. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. The scientific applications showed smaller but still notable improvements against established baselines: Cytochrome P450 is a family of enzymes involved in how the body processes drugs. 08c9672b38.title: Google DeepMind Agent Teams Discover Lean-Verified Quantum Algorithms
08c9672b38.summary: Google DeepMind presented research on November 23, 2026 showing that teams of Gemini 4 agents, checked by the Lean theorem prover, produced lower-cost quantum programs for five problems. Its largest scientific gain was an 11.8-fold reduction in the estimated cost of a fusion simulation, in work with Google Quantum AI. The work covered parallel Grover search, fixed-point arcsin arithmetic and three simulations: alpha-particle stopping power in fusion fuel, non-Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics and Cytochrome P450 energy estimation. For fault-tolerant circuits, researchers measured spacetime cost as peak logical qubits multiplied by T-gate count, combining memory demand with operations that are costly in error-corrected quantum computers. Quantum algorithm discovery has an evaluation problem: candidates spanning hundreds or thousands of qubits generally cannot be tested through classical simulation or on present quantum processors. DeepMind’s system therefore treats a proposed circuit as a mathematical object. Researchers wrote frozen Lean specifications containing correctness and resource-cost theorems; agents supplied programs, cost bounds and proofs, using high-level optimization prompts rather than problem-specific starting ideas. The large autonomous runs used Gemini 4 Carbon models. The Lean 4 library is grounded in quantum Hoare logic, a logic for reasoning about preconditions and postconditions, and handles classical control flow alongside unitary operations, measurement and qubit reset. It can prove bounds on expected or worst-case resource costs. An external verifier replayed every submission in a clean sandbox against the frozen specification, checking dependent definitions, permitted axioms and claimed costs to prevent agents from weakening theorems or otherwise gaming local checks. Independent teams shared their best verified solutions, reusable lemmas and reviewed dead-end notes through a wiki, while agents met every four hours in virtual conferences to critique proposals. Conference claims counted only after verification. The paper estimates that, averaged across the three scientific applications, 61% of the measured cost reduction originated within teams, 15% came through cross-team wiki material and 24% through conferences, while cautioning that credit is difficult to separate cleanly. For fusion stopping power, the discovered circuit moves electron interactions onto a real-space grid and uses Pauli exclusion to simplify short-range…

8a5a53834d.title: DeepMind AI Quantum Algorithms: 290× arcsin, Lean Proof
8a5a53834d.summary: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI used teams of Gemini 4 agents to shrink expensive quantum circuits — and proved the results in Lean. In a November 23, 2026 post , Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, and Ryan Babbush describe agent teams that debate ideas, share a notebook, and pass Lean verification before a candidate counts. Reported wins include 11.8× lower cost for inertial confinement fusion math, 8× for a photochemistry molecule, 2.5× for Cytochrome P450 , 2.57× on a Grover implementation, and 290× on arcsin loading. The arXiv preprint and GitHub library ship the artifacts. This is not a Willow chip benchmark. It is algorithm design under proof , aimed at science problems quantum hardware may eventually run. For AI builders, the reusable pattern is spec → multi-agent search → verifier gate → shared wiki , with humans choosing problems rather than hand-tuning circuits. DeepMind stresses that even after these cuts , full scientific runs would still exceed what first error-corrected quantum computers are likely to provide. The news is proved headroom , not a near-term lab schedule. Quantum advantage stories often stall on a boring constraint: you cannot faithfully simulate the biggest circuits on classical machines , and today's NISQ devices are too small. DeepMind's response is to make Lean the acceptance test. Agents propose circuits; Lean proves they meet specifications and resource bounds . That mirrors how AlphaEvolve used automated search for classical algorithms, but adds mathematical correctness obligations appropriate when a wrong phase break could silently invalidate a chemistry or fusion model. If you build research agents , the lesson is structural: when execution is impossible, the checker must be formal . The Into the Unknown benchmark showed how many agent papers fail when human rubrics are weak; here the rubric is machine-checked proof . Gemini agent teams improving quantum algorithm circuits per Google DeepMind November 2026 Image: Google DeepMind DeepMind's architecture assigns independent teams per problem. Each team iterates on circuit ideas, submits candidates to Lean , and writes successes into a shared notebook . Every four hours , agents from each team join a virtual conference to compare, debate, and trade improvements. That cadence is slower than a single ReAct coding loop, but it mirrors how human theory groups actually work — parallel exploration plus scheduled sync. 680d0b8ac6.summary: (CBS, KYMA) - Brad Smith, Vice Chair and President of Microsoft, spoke with Margaret Brennan on Face the Nation Sunday about the email outage. Earlier this month, a global outage disrupted several services , which included Outlook, Teams and Copilot, interrupting e-mail to users worldwide. Microsoft said the outage was due to a technical issue, and not a cyberattack, prompting Brennan to ask Smith what the company is doing to make sure it doesn't happen again, and whether AI played a role in the outage, to which he said: "The first thing we always need to do when this happens is apologize, and we have, and I want to do so again. And you're right; it was not linked to AI. It wasn't a cyberattack. It was basically a perfect storm of software that was updated four months earlier, and then it interacted with a new update and a shift in network traffic. You know, we have taken steps. We've published two reports in the last 10 days. We've worked to be transparent, showing minute by minute to the public what happened. We've taken nine steps already, as we laid out in our report. There's 13 more steps we're going to take. We've learned a lot. It was painful, especially for everybody who relies on us. We get it, and I think this combination is going to make us stronger going forward. It's just constantly what we have to do in an age of such complex technology." Following Microsoft's outage, there were several more outages, including a ground stop at airports across the country , raising questions about what AI's role is generally. 7da3f2f785.title: CyberCube estimates Microsoft 365 outage insurance losses below $100 mn, up to $350 mn
7da3f2f785.summary: CyberCube estimates that global cyber insured losses from the Microsoft 365 outage on November 12-14, 2026, will most likely total less than $100 mn, according to its preliminary catastrophe analysis. The cyber risk analytics company placed a conservative upper bound of $350 mn on potential losses, allowing for additional claims information that may emerge. CyberCube, which has nicknamed the incident “M364”, expects the event to produce insured losses equivalent to 0%-2% of global cyber insurance premiums. The assessment is consistent with the Level 2 (moderate) event classification issued to clients on November 13. Most modelled outcomes are concentrated toward the lower end of the estimated range, reflecting limited evidence of material financial disruption despite the outage’s geographical reach. Morningstar DBRS projects losses of $300 mn-$500 mn, while insurance broker Acrisure has estimated $700 mn. The disruption began on November 12 following a failure in Microsoft Exchange Online, the email infrastructure supporting Outlook. Users in more than 70 countries experienced service interruptions, while Exchange-dependent features in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and Microsoft’s security tools were also degraded. The core functions of those additional services largely remained operational. Microsoft attributed the incident to a technical problem introduced during a network capacity upgrade, rather than malicious cyber activity. Severe disruption lasted approximately 18 hours, while the overall incident continued for about 38 hours. The duration exceeded the eight- to 12-hour waiting periods commonly applied to contingent systems failure coverage, which can compensate businesses for interruption caused by non-malicious outages at external technology providers. Exceeding those waiting periods does not automatically trigger compensation. Coverage must extend to non-malicious failures at third-party providers, and policyholders must demonstrate qualifying business interruption losses. CyberCube identified several factors likely to restrict insured losses despite the incident’s duration. Reported impacts primarily involved interrupted communications, reduced productivity and inconvenience rather than demonstrable revenue losses. Alternative communication channels were widely available, allowing many businesses to continue operations while Exchange Online services were disrupted. The company also found no reported evidence of data corruption or…

cb81e96627.title: Microsoft's Outlook outage didn't take long to become phishing bait
cb81e96627.summary: Microsoft Outlook and several of the company's other services went down earlier this month. Millions of people were affected by the outage, and some were unable to receive emails for almost a full day. Scammers are aware of how widespread the outage was and are looking to take advantage of those affected. Microsoft issued a warning about a phishing campaign that tricks people into believing emails held during the outage need to be recovered. Recipients will receive an email claiming that emails have been held during a service disruption and will be deleted within 24 hours. Phishing scams often try to create a sense of urgency with false deadlines or "expiring" items. It's also normal for scammers to attach campaigns to trending news topics and tech stories. Microsoft's recent outage was one of the biggest IT events in recent memory, so many people who usually ignore tech likely saw coverage of it. Microsoft first shared its warning last week, but it has become more relevant now that the full incident report has been released . Despite the fact that many were unable to send or receive messages during the outage, Microsoft has confirmed that all emails from that time have since been delivered: "No mail was lost, and all queued messages were successfully delivered. The incident did not impact customer data at rest," said Microsoft. That means there is no pile of held emails to be released. Of course, malicious actors would have no intention of helping you. The aim of phishing scams is often to trick people into handing over account credentials or other sensitive information. Microsoft also reminded users that legitimate Microsoft 365 service health notifications do not direct people to non-Microsoft websites to recover held emails. Microsoft has not found any evidence of credentials being captured through this specific phishing campaign. Microsoft says Defender blocks the malicious domains used in the campaign, while Defender for Office 365 blocks and quarantines the phishing emails. Millions of people heard about Microsoft's outage, but many never saw Microsoft's explanation of what happened. Microsoft says every delayed email was delivered , which means there is no reason to click a link claiming your messages are waiting to be recovered . 93c14c606b.title: Nvidia surges 30% after Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO
93c14c606b.summary: Shares in Nvidia skyrocketed after the company reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, driving a broader rally on Wall Street. Nvidia soared more than 30 per cent during intraday trading, erasing almost all the losses it suffered after Mr Huang stepped down less than two weeks ago. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 jumped more than 7 and 5 per cent, respectively. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,344 points, or 2.8 per cent. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company," the chairman of Nvidia's board of directors said in a statement. Earlier this month, Mr Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive following multiple allegations of extramarital affairs, including one US officials suspect of being a spy for China . “I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Mr Huang said in a statement. Mr Huang's return is the latest twist in what has been a turbulent time for the AI industry. Disappointing earnings reports in October sparked fears about AI financing, while the Democrats' sweeping victory in the midterm elections added to fears of a slowdown in the data centre buildout. That selling pressure further intensified after Mr Huang's departure from Nvidia. A strong outlook from Nvidia's earnings last week failed to halt the downward momentum, as did Anthropic's IPO. Mr Huang's return to Nvidia pulled neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius 23 per cent higher each. Semiconductor stocks also surged. Micron and Intel were up 19 and 12 per cent, respectively, while AMD gained 8 per cent. Other members of the Magnificent 7 joined in on the rally, with Tesla up more than 12 per cent, Alphabet and Meta up roughly 6 per cent, Amazon up nearly 4 per cent, Microsoft up 2.74 per cent and Apple up about 1.7 per cent. The affair inflamed concerns in Washington that China could have been given access to Nvidia's most advanced AI chips. The US has banned the sale of those chips to China, citing national security concerns. Nvidia's board of directors said it had voted unanimously to bring Mr Huang back as chief executive after a series of discussions with Mr Huang. The chip maker said it had also received input from US government officials and concluded Mr Huang's reinstatement “poses no national security risk”. 230d0af700.title: DeepMind’s AI agents found cheaper quantum algorithms, and proved them
230d0af700.summary: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI used teams of Gemini 4 agents to find more efficient quantum algorithms for fusion, chemistry and drug-design problems. Each result was proved correct in the Lean theorem prover, because the circuits are too large to test on today’s computers. Google DeepMind says teams of AI agents have found faster quantum algorithms for problems in fusion energy, chemistry and drug design. The agents, running on Gemini 4, proved each result correct with Lean, a tool that checks mathematical proofs, the lab said on Monday. The proofs matter because the circuits are too big to test. They need thousands of qubits, far beyond what classical computers can simulate or today’s quantum chips can run. The biggest gain came in a fusion problem. The agents cut the cost of a quantum calculation for laser-driven fusion fuel by 11.8 times, and its memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits, DeepMind says. They also made a simulation of a light-sensitive molecule about eight times cheaper. For Cytochrome P450, an enzyme that breaks down most medicines, the cost fell 2.5 times. A widely used maths routine became more than 290 times cheaper. Separate agent teams worked on each problem and shared verified ideas in a common notebook. Every four hours, they met in a virtual conference to debate and compare approaches. The work, with Google Quantum AI, used Google’s most powerful model, Gemini 4 Carbon . An outside checker re-ran every proof so agents could not game the tests, according to the paper. That risk is real: in a DeepMind experiment in September, 14% of agents cheated on Lean maths problems. DeepMind cautions that the simulations would still need far more resources than the first error-corrected quantum computers will offer. It has open-sourced its Lean library and results, building on its 2024 work to trim quantum circuits with AlphaTensor-Quantum. Earlier this month, its agents also proved Signal’s encryption code correct, and Google Quantum AI tested a key quantum effect on up to 105 qubits . 5b77a90f2c.title: As tech outages mount, some New Yorkers prepare for the worst
5b77a90f2c.summary: New York City, New York – When a series of technology outages struck services across the United States this month, Kristyn Lavery began thinking about what might happen if the disruptions lasted longer. The 67-year-old retired fashion designer, who has lived in Manhattan’s East Village since 1981, started keeping cash and extra water in her 32.5-square-metre (350-square-foot) apartment. She also looked into ways to keep warm but says she cannot afford a generator, which can cost hundreds of dollars. Lavery is part of a trend of US citizens stocking up on essential supplies over fears that the technology outages could presage other vulnerabilities — or even a tech collapse. Public concern began to grow on November 13, after a malfunctioning flight communication system led to a nationwide halt to air travel. Experts later credited the ground stop to a tech update gone awry. The flight delays happened around the same time that the tech giant Microsoft announced problems with its services, including the email platform Outlook. In the following days, the US National Security Agency , the tech company Apple and banks including JPMorgan Chase all reported service disruptions. Last week, authorities said they were also investigating a suspected hack of the National Crime Information Center and the US Department of Agriculture. While there is no evidence that the episodes are connected, residents like Lavery say they are worried. For Lavery, the recent outages have heightened fears shaped by major events like the attacks on September 11, 2001, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Now, with US officials warning about further disruptions, she is determined to take the possibility of another emergency more seriously. “I feel vulnerable. And I don’t want to be a victim. Yet I feel like, if this happens, it will be on me for not preparing,” she told Al Jazeera. She remembers what happened in 2012, when flooding from Hurricane Sandy disrupted transport and power in parts of Manhattan. Her neighbourhood went without heat and hot water for days, and residents had to rely on one another. “I got no help from the government,” Lavery said. “It was neighbours helping neighbours.” The growing interest in emergency preparedness has become a trend on social media in recent weeks. 76e6087809.title: Russian ship hit by suspected drone attack at Libyan naval base
76e6087809.summary: An explosion hit a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base early on Sunday in what was believed to be a drone attack, the government of eastern Libya said. The government said the ship was returning to Russia and had stopped at Benghazi to refuel and resupply, under agreements between Russia and the eastern administration. It said the port and naval base sites were safe after a fire was brought under control. Russia is renewing its interest in Libya as Africa faces a turning point There was no claim of responsibility. Ukraine has attacked Russian interests far and wide since Moscow began its 2022 invasion, but rarely acknowledges its involvement. The local authorities said in their statement that “Libya is not a party to the Russia-Ukraine war, nor to any armed conflict beyond its own borders”. It said its “legitimate relations” with other countries were a matter for Libya. “The Libyan government will not permit its ports, territory, or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or importing international conflicts,” it said. The eastern government ordered the security and military authorities to launch an investigation and work with Russian authorities to determine the circumstances of the attack and who was responsible. It condemned the incident as a serious assault on Libya’s sovereignty and a violation of the security of its ports. The Libyan authorities said they would not treat the explosion as an accidental or isolated incident and reserved the right to take all legal measures. Libya has been beset with problems, including political instability and violence, after former leader Muammar Qaddafi was overthrown in 2011. Much of its oil production has since remained offline amid unrest. The country is run by two governments, in Tripoli and Benghazi, with the presence of numerous armed groups wielding influence and discouraging investors to inject funds into the country. Libya has the world's 10th-largest proven oil reserves at nearly 48.4 million barrels, which is also the largest in Africa, data from Worldometer shows.

9a843b0cbb.title: OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits
9a843b0cbb.summary: OpenAI ties capabilities like fluent conversation and math breakthroughs to specific scores. For the first time, chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is showing where the GPT series sits on that scale, up to an unreleased model beyond GPT-6. Pachocki wants to make perplexity a common measure of progress for the AI industry and published internal scores for the GPT series in a bl o g post . The metric has long been standard in AI research and Transformer development because it reliably measures how well a pretrained base model predicts the next token in a text. Lower scores mean more accurate predictions. A perplexity of 2 roughly means the model is as uncertain about the next token as if it were choosing between two equally likely options. Before it stopped publishing openly, OpenAI often released perplexity scores to show how its models were improving. Releasing them again is a trade-off, Pachocki writes . While rivals get a clearer picture of where OpenAI stands, he says, the need for shared safety standards outweighs that downside. He hopes for a common scientific foundation that lets labs coordinate their pace of development at critical points. Pachocki says many capabilities of modern models map surprisingly closely to specific perplexity scores, even though it wasn't clear beforehand that they would appear at those thresholds. He reports the figures on a logarithmic scale called log-perplexity, where lower scores are still better. In his account, GPT-3.5 first enabled fluent conversation at around 0.99, laying the groundwork for the original ChatGPT. At about 0.91, GPT-4 unlocked productive chain-of-thought reasoning, or working through problems step by step. Below 0.8, he writes, transformative capabilities emerged in cybersecurity and math . The published chart plots OpenAI's base-model log-perplexity by release or evaluation date through November 2026. It covers GPT-5 , GPT-5.1 , GPT-5.2 , GPT-5.3-Codex , GPT-5.4 , GPT-5.5 , GPT-5.6 Sol , GPT-6 Astra , and GPT-6.2 Astra , plus an internal model at around 0.73. OpenAI has been feeding its models open math problems for more than a year. Starting with a model at about 0.76 log-perplexity, the models began producing breakthrough results, Pachocki writes. For researchers with a math background, he says, it was "deeply surreal" to watch solutions to longstanding questions pop up one after another in a single Slack thread. d17e7b7013.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
d17e7b7013.summary: An open-source runtime that helps operators protect running Linux systems without needing to wait for the patch or restarts OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches. In a controlled test ⁠ (opens in a new window) , a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart. We’re inviting developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators across the industry to help develop the project further. The project brings together OpenAI’s frontier AI, security and infrastructure research and Cisco’s infrastructure and security expertise to help protect the systems people rely on every day. Testing and deploying a patch can still take days or weeks. Protecting a service in the meantime can be challenging because an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same Linux operation. Blocking that operation entirely could take the service offline. Shirudo (Japanese for “shield”) is designed to help security teams navigate this tradeoff. Teams can test whether a temporary safeguard, called a shield, blocks the behavior that exposes a vulnerability while allowing legitimate requests through. Once an operator approves the shield, it can be deployed while the service continues running. Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system. This makes it possible to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted security protections to running systems. OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo around four core capabilities: Live protection: eBPF shields can block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system. Security teams can monitor how a proposed shield would affect applications before enforcing it. Defense at machine speed: OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo to give agents programmable controls to investigate vulnerabilities, develop targeted shields, and validate their effectiveness against exploits and real workloads. Security teams control what gets deployed. Trusted deployment: Shields are cryptographically signed and verified before loading. Linux's eBPF verifier checks eBPF programs against its safety rules, while kernel security controls restrict unauthorized changes. Hardware-backed verification: Shirudo uses a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) to support a verifiable record of protections being loaded or removed.…

e310da3525.title: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
e310da3525.summary: Cybercriminals have gained the ability to discover vulnerabilities in software and take advantage of them in seconds, and it’s all thanks to artificial intelligence . Enterprises need a better way to defend themselves, so it’s fitting that one of the world’s top AI companies, OpenAI Group PBC, together with Cisco Systems Inc., is stepping up with a solution. They’ve just announced a new, open-source and extremely ambitious initiative called the Secure Infrastructure Project, which aims to ensure that all AI computing infrastructure is secure by design and capable of defending against lightning-fast AI-driven attacks. The first project within that initiative is Shirudo, which is designed to protect infrastructure systems automatically from critical exploits before they can be patched. In a blog post, Cisco Security Chief Technology Officer and Vice President of Engineering Thomas Graf explained that the industry has always treated security as an afterthought, essentially something that’s bolted onto systems after the fact. It has gotten away with this because much of the world’s computing infrastructure was built for workflows that proceed at human speeds. But with the emergence of AI models that can discover and work out how to exploit vulnerabilities in a matter of seconds, this kind of reactive security is no longer enough. According to Graf, even now, when a major vulnerability is discovered in widely used software, it can take weeks or even months to come up with a fix and ensure that every major system is patched against it. “That timeframe is no longer acceptable given that the mean time to exploitation has become negative, meaning that a growing number of vulnerabilities are now being exploited before they are publicly disclosed,” he said. “This will only accelerate with the further evolution of AI models and cybersecurity capabilities, becoming the norm in open-weight models.” To counter these kinds of automated attacks, Cisco and OpenAI believe that infrastructure has to be rebuilt from scratch with security in mind. They argue that it’s time to abandon static defenses and embrace systems that are hardened by default, immutable and rebuildable from a previous “good” state, so users can quickly revert back in the event of an attack. 624cd70034.title: OpenAI Pitches Perplexity Score to Set AI Safety Limits
624cd70034.summary: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed perplexity, a metric for how well a model predicts text, as a common score for comparing AI models and setting shared limits on development. A lower score means better predictions, and OpenAI’s log-perplexity score fell from about 0.99 for GPT-3.5 to below 0.8, as math and cybersecurity skills emerged. Google DeepMind researchers say a low score does not prove accuracy, while Microsoft’s AI chief says labs’ scores are not directly comparable. Pachocki set no first limit or date. Artificial intelligence developers often learn what a new model can do only after they have built it. OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki wants the industry to watch one metric that he says tracks how intelligent a model is, and to agree on limits tied to that metric until safety tools catch up. The metric is perplexity (not the AI search company of the same name), which measures how well a model predicts the next token, or piece of text, on average. A lower score means better predictions. A large language model learns by reading huge amounts of text, split into tokens that are words or pieces of words, and guessing which token comes next. Perplexity measures how good those guesses are on text the model was not trained on. In a Sunday (Nov. 22) blog post titled “Perplexity and Intelligence,” Pachocki proposed that AI developers use perplexity to compare progress across companies and to set shared safety standards. The post also calls for common limits that developers commit not to cross until researchers can better understand and monitor AI behavior, PYMNTS reported . OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wrote on X that the post is “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while.” GPT-3.5, which powered the original ChatGPT, had a log-perplexity score of about 0.99. GPT-4 reached about 0.91, alongside improvements in reasoning capabilities. More recent models have brought that measurement below 0.8, coinciding with advances in mathematics and cybersecurity. Pachocki wrote that a model at about 0.76 produced “groundbreaking results” on open math problems. OpenAI has posed such problems to its models as a test for more than a year, he wrote. On Sept. 8, OpenAI said an unreleased model solved the Navier-Stokes problem on fluid flow, one of seven Millennium Prize Problems. 27065c561f.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
27065c561f.summary: Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship , a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes. The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team. The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself. “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.” Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge. The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available , and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed. Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language. Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process. b4480ae580.title: Google DeepMind Agent Swarm Optimizes Quantum Algorithms, Arcsin Subroutine Speeds Up 290-Fold
b4480ae580.summary: Google DeepMind and the Google Quantum AI team jointly released research findings on November 23, using multiple Gemini 4 agents working in concert and introducing the formal mathematical verification tool Lean to optimize several classic quantum algorithms, sharply reducing the hardware resources required for some quantum computing tasks. The related paper, problem definition files, and verified solutions have been open-sourced on GitHub for the academic community to reuse. Quantum computers are expected to solve problems that classical supercomputers struggle to tackle, but even with current state-of-the-art algorithms, some key applications require far more resources than early quantum hardware can bear. The research team's approach was to have a team of agents automatically search for more efficient quantum circuits—the instruction sets a quantum computer executes to run an algorithm—and to prove their correctness mathematically. Because such resource-intensive circuits cannot be tested on classical computers or existing small-scale quantum processors, formal verification becomes essential to confirming the reliability of the results. According to IT之家 (ITHome), the agent teams pursued optimization independently, converging and exchanging ideas in a virtual environment every four hours to form an iterative improvement process. Researchers only needed to specify the research direction, define the problems, and supervise progress; combined with their own expertise in quantum algorithms, they could produce verifiable scientific results. On the application side, the team prioritized scenarios tied to major challenges such as clean energy and drug design. For the calculation of key properties of inertial confinement fusion—a fusion approach that uses lasers to compress hydrogen fuel until ignition—the optimized quantum circuit reduced compute cost (a metric combining qubit count and operation count) by 11.8-fold, and the number of error-corrected qubits required fell from 5,650 to 4,338. Progress was also made in molecular simulation: for common photosensitive molecules, quantum simulation cost fell 8-fold, and the algorithm's logic for tracking particle positions and electric field forces was simplified; for cytochrome P450 enzymes, which break down most human drugs and are crucial to drug design, the team achieved a 2.5-fold performance improvement by replacing redundant memory lookup operations, cutting memory footprint from 481 qubits to 333. 9fa5edc42f.title: AWS Faces Customer Backlash Over 93-Minute Delay in Outage Alert
9fa5edc42f.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has come under criticism for delaying its notification of a major data center service outage that lasted nearly four hours. According to major international media reports on Nov. 23, an outage occurred in AWS's US East (us-east-1) region, one of its largest and most critical infrastructure hubs, at 3:05 a.m. local time on Nov. 15. The disruption lasted about three hours and 48 minutes, affecting more than 10 major AWS services through sign-up errors, authentication failures and connectivity issues. Services were not fully restored until 6:53 a.m. The controversy centers on AWS's handling of incident communications. Although AWS engineers began responding within five minutes of the outage, the company did not post its first official notification on its customer-facing status page until 93 minutes after the disruption began. The outage attracted relatively little media and public attention. It occurred early on a Sunday morning and was overshadowed by other major disruptions, including a Microsoft 365 outage on Nov. 13 and a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) air traffic control system failure that caused a nationwide suspension of flight operations in the United States. Another factor limiting public attention was that the disruption primarily affected IAM Identity Center, an authentication system used by enterprise developers, rather than consumer-facing applications. For enterprise customers, however, the delay meant spending more than 90 minutes without even knowing the cause of the disruption. International media outlets also criticized AWS's defensive response. According to technology publication The Register, when signs of the AWS outage appeared on the real-time outage reporting platform Downdetector, the company focused on questioning the platform's reliability rather than explaining its own system failures. Downdetector serves as a reference tool for users seeking to determine whether service problems stem from their own systems or a broader infrastructure outage. In March this year, Accenture acquired Ookla, Downdetector's parent company, from Ziff Davis Media.

34a332f08c.title: Anthropic is betting AI can help conquer disease and generate big bucks in the bargain
34a332f08c.summary: Fresh off its record-setting initial public offering , Anthropic now must show investors that it can sustain growth and generate profits. The company has a plan for that: curing some of the world's gnarliest diseases. In its IPO prospectus, Anthropic states that AI holds the potential to "profoundly accelerate the rate of progress in biology and medicine, potentially curing diseases that have plagued humanity for millennia, including cancer, Alzheimer's disease, heart disease, rare genetic diseases, and the major infectious diseases." Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei said in a post on X in August that he believes "it will actually be possible to cure most human disease in ~5-10 years, as crazy as it may sound to ordinary people and frankly to biologists as well (I used to be one!)." Developing breakthrough drugs is among the most promising avenues of research for AI, potentially bringing treatments for a range of conditions to market much faster than is currently possible, according to scientists and industry analysts. "AI can accelerate research. It will help you get there faster, but it's not just speed — it's directional speed," Neerav Kaushal, an AI and molecular biology expert at Michigan Technological University, told CBS News. "Let's say you're at the top of the mountain and your aim is to find a drug for cancer that lies in the valley. AI will not just help you get down there faster — it will help you get down to the right valley where the drug is." For Anthropic, meanwhile, developing drugs could open up potentially enormous commercial opportunities. The company has partnered with biotech and pharmaceutical companies that use its Claude Science model for various purposes. Anthropic also operates its own AI-powered biology wet lab in San Francisco that has already made scientific discoveries. "If you can use a large language model to condense any part of the timeline, it is very economically valuable," Morningstar senior equity analyst Malik Ahmed Khan told CBS News. The challenge for Anthropic will be how it turns its life sciences research into profits. That could take time, Khan told CBS News. "How this becomes lucrative for Anthropic is a very important question, and I think it's a question Anthropic hasn't figured out yet," Khan said.
