07b4e95a07.title: Working with AI
07b4e95a07.summary: Nathan Wilmers, Maxim Massenkoff, Peter McCrory How are businesses across the economy adopting AI? What bottlenecks and challenges have they faced? How can employers reorganize human expertise around increasingly capable models? To understand businesses’ experiences better, we conducted 66 interviews with 58 of Anthropic’s enterprise customers. We found: The use of LLMs has exploded across the economy. How are human organizations reshaping around these strange new collaborators? Consider an employee at a midsize law firm that we spoke to. For years, the firm’s mailroom had followed the same protocol: a scanner sent PDFs of incoming correspondence to an inbox; a mail clerk opened each PDF, skimmed it, clicked “Save As,” renamed it, and placed it in the firm’s file system. The process took five minutes per letter. One day, a senior developer visited the mailroom to watch the mail being processed. In a month, he built an AI system that eventually became two API calls, which name the document based on its first page and then assign it a place in the firm’s document system. The mail clerks “were blown away.” An employee at another law firm we interviewed hoped AI would create “a second brain” for the firm. (“For higher-level stuff, it just opens up possibilities.”) But the firm struggled to get everyone to use AI effectively. Demand letters to potential defendants were filled with excessive em dashes and occasional errors. Attorneys building apps kept “running into the wall based on hallucinated menus or buttons that don’t exist.” Others worried about confidentiality and data security, or they just didn’t “have time to get onto this AI train.” A few power users inundated the firm with AI prose, “casually sending Claude-prompted seven-page instructions to the IT team.” A third law firm we spoke to adopted AI early and achieved strong uptake. One of the firm’s early projects was an AI timekeeping system that saved attorneys work tracking billable hours. IT staff saw parts of their job automated, but they then focused on building secure infrastructure to host apps and manage context that served the rest of the firm. As AI tools spread, the firm realized that associates were no longer needed to write first drafts of certain legal documents. 100532987a.title: Power outage causes brief delay for 'Monday Night Football'
100532987a.summary: The "Monday Night Football" game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders was delayed because of a power outage. The lights went out at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland, for a few minutes in the third quarter as the Commanders were facing a third-and-14. Video above: How Jeopardy game helps Bengals QBs prepare for the spotlight The visiting Bengals held a slight 10-7 lead as Washington was about to attempt a passing play to keep its drive alive. The ESPN broadcast said the issue was not stadium-specific, but rather due to power issues in the immediate area around the stadium. After a few minutes, power was restored. The Commanders' next play was an unsuccessful third-down attempt. Washington's Drew Stevens then connected on a field goal try from 36 yards out to tie the game at 10. Stevens proved to be the hero later in the game when he nailed a 26-yard field goal as time expired to secure a 22-20 Commanders' win over Cincinnati. The loss snapped the Bengals’ five-game winning streak. The Bengals fell to 8-3 with the loss but maintain a one-game lead in the AFC North. Washington is now 4-5-1.

3bb9c8524c.title: What do we know about the strike on Libya's Benghazi port?
3bb9c8524c.summary: Satellite imagery and video footage show that at least two Russian vessels were struck in and around Libya's Benghazi port, with evidence of damage at several locations. Ukraine claimed responsibility for the attack on Monday. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces used seven domestically made naval drones to target the warship. He said the Merkury was sunk despite Russian efforts to repel the attack, and claimed a Ka-27 military helicopter was also destroyed. Footage of the operation was filmed from cameras mounted on its sea drones and from nearby cameras. The National examined that footage alongside satellite imagery and other available evidence to piece together what happened. The first clip in the sequence, filmed at night using a thermal camera mounted on the front of a drone, shows the drone approaching a grey warship moored alongside a quay. Seconds later, a large explosion engulfs the vessel. Satellite imagery from Vantor gives us a clearer picture of the aftermath. The Merkury is now capsized, with only its bow remaining above the water. Scorch marks are also visible across the dock, indicating the extent of the fire. The government of eastern Libya said the ship had stopped in Benghazi to refuel while returning to Russia. Medical sources told Reuters that 10 Russian and Libyan nationals sustained minor injuries. But the Merkury wasn't the only vessel attacked. Hours later, another ship was struck off the coast of Benghazi. Mr Zelenskyy identified it as the MV Angara, a dry cargo vessel that he said Russia used to transport weapons. Again, Ukraine's footage shows a drone racing towards a red-hulled cargo ship before hitting its side. The National also assessed an image of a naval drone shared on social media, which appears to have been photographed inside the harbour and reportedly failed to detonate. We geolocated the position of this vessel, which is in the same location as the other detonations. Its shape, paintwork and lack of an outboard motor point strongly to a Ukrainian-made vessel. The attack has implications beyond Libya. Russia has five Project 20380 corvettes in its Baltic Fleet. Two have now been struck by Ukraine: the Boikiy, attacked in Kronstadt, and the Merkury, hit in Benghazi. The Steregushchiy is currently undergoing a refit, and the other two vessels are the Soobrazitelny and Stoikiy. 3b0cdeee2a.title: Gaza turned into ‘toxic wasteland with human survival under threat’
3b0cdeee2a.summary: Israel’s war on Gaza has caused the potential environmental contamination of more than 99 per cent of the territory, threatening human survival, a report by Oxfam has found. It said the extensive use of explosive and incendiary weapons has made air, soil and water in the strip dangerous for decades to come. Israel had “wreaked havoc” on environmental systems, “dismantling the basic conditions necessary for life”, Oxfam said. The people behind a push to promote Palestinian products The charity group's research found the scale and intensity of the Israeli military’s onslaught has affected about 78 per cent of Gaza’s land area, with potential contamination across more than 99 per cent of the territory. It said: “In this wasteland, the very conditions of civilian survival have been systematically degraded, raising grave concerns of human rights violations and breaches of international law.” “Since October 2023, Israel’s military has subjected Gaza to a sustained military assault of extraordinary scale and intensity, inflicting a humanitarian and environmental catastrophe through the excessive use of explosive weapons in one of the most densely populated areas in the world. “Hazardous contaminants have been released into the soil, water and air from munitions, destroyed buildings and infrastructure, [causing] fires, damaged industrial facilities and collapsed environmental systems. These contaminants will have profound and lasting consequences for the health of the entire population and the environmental resources upon which their lives depend.” Its report, in collaboration with the Conflict and Environment Observatory, was compiled using satellite data, remote sensing analysis and geolocated conflict incidents to map contamination risks across Gaza, and unearth the potential health consequences and legal implications of environmental harm. It found explosions and fires, together with the destruction and burning of buildings and infrastructure, have released airborne contaminants that settle on to rubble, soil and other surfaces, and are repeatedly redistributed by wind, vehicle movement and the clearance of damaged buildings and debris. The Palestinian enclave's highest concentration of air contaminants was found in Gaza city, Jabalia and the North Gaza governorate. 33d9f3879e.summary: WASHINGTON — US President Donald Trump is facing backlash for pushing Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO.Nvidia announced on Monday that Huang would be returning as its CEO just days after rejecting his offer to return to the AI chipmaker and less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over a reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy.The company came under pressure from Trump to reappoint Huang and on Monday, the US president said he "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to bring him back.But now both Trump and Nvidia are facing bipartisan backlash from lawmakers, just as Huang is due to testify before Congress next week.The CEO's comeback helped end a week-long losing streak in US stocks that left the S&P 500 in correction territory, and added nearly $1 trillion to Nvidia's market value.Board Chairman Harvey C Jones said in a statement earlier in the day: "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers."The board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.Trump reportedly enlisted Vice President JD Vance to tell Nvidia's board that Huang's return would not pose a threat to national security.Minutes after Nvidia’s announcement, Trump celebrated it with a statement on Truth Social, describing it as the “correct and proper decision” while arguing that Huang’s leadership is critical to ensuring the success of Nvidia and the US economy.Huang resigned from Nvidia on 12 November following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman, Alice Huang, who was alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence.On Monday, the US Commerce Department announced it was preparing to blacklist Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia customer where Alice Huang was CEO.In a brief interview with CNBC on Monday, Trump said he had spoken to Nvidia's board of directors and "convinced" them to bring back Huang. Trump praised the Nvidia board for acting "really responsibly" in reinstating the CEO."They did ask for assurance on the national security threat," Trump said. "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know. And we know a lot.""People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it's a threat to lose him," the president added.The president was asked whether Nvidia stock losses after Huang resigned last week…

cc10ecf774.summary: واردات الصين من الذهب تسجل مستوى قياسيا عند 209 مليارات دولار وتدعم ارتداد الأسعار عالميا. للاطلاع على أسعار الذهب أولا بأول اضغط هنا لزيارة موقع رؤيا أسعار الذهب. ارْتَفَعَتْ أَسْعَارُ الذَّهَبِ لِلْجَلْسَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ عَلَى التَّوَالِي، يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءَ، إِذْ أَعَادَتْ عَوْدَةُ جِنْسِنَ هْوَانْغَ إِلَى مَنْصِبِ الرَّئِيسِ التَّنْفِيذِيِّ لِشَرِكَةِ "إِنْفِيدْيَا" (Nvidia) الزَّخَمَ إِلَى اسْتِثْمَارَاتِ الذَّكَاءِ الِاصْطِنَاعِيِّ، مَا أَسْهَمَ فِي دَعْمِ الْأَسْوَاقِ الْوَاسِعَةِ وَتَعْزِيزِ السَّبَائِكِ الذَّهَبِيَّةِ فِي أَعْقَابِ التَّرَاجُعِ الْحَادِّ الْأَخِيرِ، بِحَسَبِ بَيَانَاتِ مَوْقِعِ "إِنْفِسْتِنْغ دُوتْ كُوم" (Investing.com). وَسَجَّلَ الذَّهَبُ الْفَوْرِيُّ ارْتِفَاعًا بِنِسْبَةِ تِسْعَةٍ بِالْعَشَرَةِ بِالْمِئَةِ لِيَبْلُغَ ثَلَاثَةَ آلَافٍ وَسِتَّمِئَةٍ وَثَمَانِيَةً وَسِتِّينَ دُولَارًا وَثَلَاثَةً وَتِسْعِينَ سِنْتًا لِلْأُوقِيَّةِ عِنْدَ السَّاعَةِ الثَّانِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ وَالنِّصْفِ وَدَقِيقَةٍ صَبَاحًا بِتَوْقِيتِ الْمَمْلَكَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ السُّعُودِيَّةِ، فِيمَا رَبِحَتْ عُقُودُ الذَّهَبِ الْأَمْرِيكِيَّةُ الْآجِلَةُ أَرْبَعَةً بِالْعَشَرَةِ بِالْمِئَةِ لِتَبْلُغَ ثَلَاثَةَ آلَافٍ وَسِتَّمِئَةٍ وَسَبْعَةً وَسِتِّينَ دُولَارًا وَخَمْسَةً وَعِشْرِينَ سِنْتًا، وَذَلِكَ بِالتَّزَامُنِ مَعَ انْخِفَاضِ مُؤَشِّرِ الدُّولَارِ الْأَمْرِيكِيِّ بِنِسْبَةِ وَاحِدٍ بِالْعَشَرَةِ بِالْمِئَةِ إِلَى مِئَةٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَوَاحِدٍ وَعِشْرِينَ بِالْمِئَةِ نُقْطَةٍ. وَعَلَى صَعِيدِ الْمَعَادِنِ النَّفِيسَةِ الْأُخْرَى، صَعِدَتِ الْفِضَّةُ بِنِسْبَةِ وَاحِدٍ وَاثْنَيْنِ بِالْعَشَرَةِ بِالْمِئَةِ إِلَى ثَلَاثَةٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ دُولَارًا وَسِتِّمِئَةٍ وَأَرْبَعَةٍ وَسِتِّينَ جُزْءًا مِنَ الْأَلْفِ لِلْأُوقِيَّةِ، فِيمَا أَضَافَ الْبِلَاتِينُ اثْنَيْنِ بِالْعَشَرَةِ بِالْمِئَةِ لِيَصِلَ إِلَى أَلْفٍ وَثَلَاثِمِئَةٍ وَاثْنَيْنِ وَثَلَاثِينَ دُولَارًا وَتِسْعَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ سِنْتًا، وَارْتَفَعَ الْبِلَادْيُومُ الْفَوْرِيُّ بِنِسْبَةِ وَاحِدٍ وَثَلَاثَةٍ بِالْعَشَرَةِ بِالْمِئَةِ إِلَى تِسْعِمِئَةٍ وَتِسْعَةِ دُولَارَاتٍ وَوَاحِدٍ وَسِتِّينَ سِنْتًا، بَيْنَمَا صَعِدَتْ عُقُودُ الْبِلَادْيُومِ الْآجِلَةُ بِنِسْبَةِ وَاحِدٍ وَوَاحِدٍ بِالْعَشَرَةِ بِالْمِئَةِ إِلَى تِسْعِمِئَةٍ وَثَلَاثَةِ دُولَارَاتٍ وَخَمْسَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ سِنْتًا. وَقَفَزَ الذَّهَبُ بِنِسْبَةٍ تَصِلُ إِلَى وَاحِدٍ بِالْمِئَةِ نَحْوَ مُسْتَوَى ثَلَاثَةِ آلَافٍ وَسِتِّمِئَةٍ وَسَبْعِينَ دُولَارًا، بَعْدَ أَنْ سَجَّلَ مَكَاسِبَ بَلَغَتْ اثْنَيْنِ وَسَبْعَةً بِالْعَشَرَةِ بِالْمِئَةِ فِي الْجَلْسَةِ السَّابِقَةِ، لِيُسْهِمَ هَذَا الِارْتِدَادُ الَّذِي امْتَدَّ يَوْمَيْنِ فِي تَعْوِيضِ…

166ff2dcee.title: إنفيديا تعيد جنسن هوانغ لقيادة الشركة بالإجماع وسهمها يقفز 31% وسط ترحيب من ترمب
166ff2dcee.summary: مجلس إدارة إنفيديا يؤكد ثقته بجنسن هوانغ بعد تلقي معطيات من مستويات عليا في الحكومة الأمريكية. أَعْلَنَتْ شَرِكَةُ "إِنْفِيدْيَا" (Nvidia) عَنْ عَوْدَةِ مُؤَسِّسِهَا الْمُشَارِكِ جِنْسِنَ هْوَانْغَ لِقِيَادَةِ الشَّرِكَةِ مِنْ جَدِيدٍ بِقَرَارٍ إِجْمَاعِيٍّ مِنْ مَجْلِسِ الْإِدَارَةِ، وَذَلِكَ بَعْدَ أَنْ كَانَ قَدْ غَادَرَ مَنْصِبَهُ فِي الثَّانِي عَشَرَ مِنْ نُوفَمْبَرَ الْجَارِي فِي أَعْقَابِ سِلْسِلَةٍ مِنَ الْفَضَائِحِ وَالتَّقَارِيرِ الَّتِي تَنَاوَلَتْ عِدَّةَ عَلَاقَاتٍ شَخْصِيَّةٍ لَهُ، مِنْ بَيْنِهَا عَلَاقَةٌ مَعَ امْرَأَةٍ مُتَّهَمَةٍ بِكَوْنِهَا جَاسُوسَةً صِينِيَّةً. وَأَوْضَحَ مَجْلِسُ إِدَارَةِ "إِنْفِيدْيَا" أَنَّ قَرَارَ إِعَادَةِ تَعْيِينِ هْوَانْغَ جَاءَ عَقِبَ "سِلْسِلَةٍ مِنَ الْمُنَاقَشَاتِ وَالِاجْتِمَاعَاتِ مَعَهُ"، خَرَجَ مِنْهَا الْمَجْلِسُ مُقْتَنِعًا بِ"صَرَاحَتِهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ عَلَى الْقِيَادَةِ"، مُؤَكِّدًا أَنَّهُ تَلَقَّى "مُعْطَيَاتٍ مِنْ مُسْتَوَيَاتٍ عُلْيَا فِي الْحُكُومَةِ الْأَمْرِيكِيَّةِ" جَعَلَتْهُ "وَاثِقًا" مِنْ أَنَّ هْوَانْغَ لَا يُشَكِّلُ خَطَرًا عَلَى الْأَمْنِ الْقَوْمِيِّ، وَذَلِكَ بَعْدَ أَنْ جَادَلَ مُنْتَقِدُونَ بِأَنَّ عَلَاقَتَهُ بِامْرَأَةٍ مُتَّهَمَةٍ بِالتَّجَسُّسِ لِصَالِحِ الصِّينِ قَدْ تُقَوِّضُ جُهُودَ أَمْرِيكَا لِمَنْعِ اسْتِحْوَاذِ الصِّينِ عَلَى رَقَائِقِهَا الْإِلِكْتْرُونِيَّةِ الْمِحْوَرِيَّةِ لِتِكْنُولُوجْيَا الذَّكَاءِ الِاصْطِنَاعِيِّ. وَقَالَ رَئِيسُ مَجْلِسِ الْإِدَارَةِ هَارْفِي سِي جُونْزُ إِنَّ الْمَجْلِسَ يُؤْمِنُ بِأَنَّ جِنْسِنَ هُوَ الشَّخْصُ الْمُنَاسِبُ لِقِيَادَةِ الشَّرِكَةِ وَأَنَّ إِعَادَتَهُ تَصُبُّ فِي مَصْلَحَةِ الْمُسَاهِمِينَ وَالْمُوَظَّفِينَ وَالشُّرَكَاءِ وَالْعُمَلَاءِ، فِيمَا أَعْرَبَ هْوَانْغُ عَنْ شُعُورِهِ بِ"الشَّرَفِ" لِلْعَوْدَةِ مُضِيفًا: "أَتَوَلَّى هَذِهِ الْمَسْؤُولِيَّةَ بِمُنْتَهَى التَّوَاضُعِ وَالْتِزَامٍ مُتَجَدِّدٍ". وَجَاءَ إِعْلَانُ "إِنْفِيدْيَا" بَعْدَ حَمْلَةِ ضُغُوطٍ وَدَعَوَاتٍ مُتَوَاصِلَةٍ مِنْ قَادَةٍ فِي قِطَاعِ التِّكْنُولُوجْيَا، مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ إِيلُونُ مَاسْكُ، وَمِنْ دُونَالْدَ تْرَمْبَ الَّذِي صَرَّحَ قَبْلَ سَاعَاتٍ مِنَ الْإِعْلَانِ بِأَنَّ إِعَادَةَ تَوْظِيفِ هْوَانْغَ سَتَكُونُ "أَفْضَلَ شَيْءٍ لِلشَّرِكَةِ، وَكَذَلِكَ لِلْوِلَايَاتِ الْمُتَّحِدَةِ الْأَمْرِيكِيَّةِ"، فَضْلًا عَنْ عَرِيضَةٍ دَاعِمَةٍ حَصَدَتْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ مِئَتَيْ أَلْفِ تَوْقِيعٍ، بِمَنْ فِيهِمْ أَشْخَاصٌ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُمْ مُوَظَّفُونَ وَمُسْتَثْمِرُونَ فِي الشَّرِكَةِ، مَا دَفَعَ هْوَانْغَ الْأُسْبُوعَ الْمَاضِي، بَعْدَ خَمْسَةِ أَيَّامٍ مِنْ رَحِيلِهِ، إِلَى إِعْلَانِ اسْتِعْدَادِهِ لِلْعَوْدَةِ إِذَا طَلَبَ الْمَجْلِسُ ذَلِكَ. اقرأ أيضاً: ترمب يكشف…

aaf174d238.title: Amazon, Decart'ı 7,5 milyar dolara satın aldı
aaf174d238.summary: Amazon 'un Decart 'ı 7,5 milyar dolara kadar ulaşabilecek bir bedelle satın almak için görüşmeler yürüttüğünü sizlere aktarmıştık . Söz konusu satın alma haberi doğrulandı . Anlaşma kapsamında Amazon, Decart'ın yapay zeka modellerinin farklı donanımlarda daha verimli çalışmasını sağlayan Decart Optimization Stack (DOS) teknolojisini bünyesine katacak. Satın alma, şirketin kurucu ekibinin yanı sıra yapay zeka alanında çalışan araştırmacı ve mühendisleri de kapsıyor. Amazon'un Decart'a ilgisinin arkasında, kendi geliştirdiği Trainium çiplerini Nvidia'ya karşı daha güçlü bir alternatif haline getirme hedefi bulunuyor. Şirket, bugüne kadar Trainium çiplerini kendi veri merkezlerinde kullanıyordu. Şimdi ise bu çipleri müşterilerine sunmaya hazırlanıyor. Decart'ın optimizasyon teknolojisi, geliştiricilerin yapay zeka iş yüklerini Nvidia GPU'ları yerine Amazon'un Trainium çiplerinde çalıştırmasını kolaylaştırabilir. Amazon'da temel yapay zeka modelleri, özel çipler ve kuantum bilişimden sorumlu kıdemli başkan yardımcısı Peter DeSantis, daha verimli hesaplama altyapısının model eğitimi, pekiştirmeli öğrenme ve çıkarım süreçlerini hızlandıracağını belirtiyor. DeSantis'e göre bu verimlilik, müşterilere daha düşük maliyetle daha gelişmiş modeller sunulmasının da önünü açabilir. Amazon ve Decart, anlaşmanın finansal koşullarına ilişkin ek bir açıklama yapmadı.

19564affd4.title: Iran's President works in dim office in winter jacket as power cuts hit
19564affd4.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has been filmed working in a dimly lit office while wearing a winter jacket, as electricity cuts are imposed amid mounting power shortages. In footage broadcast on state TV, a reporter visits Mr Pezeshkian's office to show how he is adhering to his calls for the public to conserve energy. Lights in the office are largely switched off, but there is daylight. Heating and air conditioning are also kept to a minimum. Investigation Iran's 'missile cities': Did western tunnelling equipment help dig them? Mr Pezeshkian, who wears a jacket while working at his desk, said the government must lead by example. "Look, with just a little light, and by wearing warm clothes, people's work can still get done," he said in the footage. "There's enough light. There's no need to switch on all these lights just to do your job. And if it gets very cold, we can move into a smaller room and bring our colleagues together in one place." Iran has started to impose scheduled power cuts on consumers because of difficulties supplying fuel to power plants, state electricity company Tavanir said. The restrictions were initially expected to last up to two hours every other day, rising to two hours daily if temperatures dropped further, Tavanir chief executive Mohammad Allahdad told state television on Sunday. "Given the country's fuel supply conditions, the electricity sector will be forced to impose distribution restrictions from Sunday," he said. The duration of the power cuts would depend on fuel availability and the extent to which consumers managed their energy use, Mr Allahdad added. Iran has imposed similar cuts in recent years when power plants ran short of fuel. Its electricity grid has also suffered from years of underinvestment, while rising household demand for gas for winter heating has increased pressure on energy supplies. The latest restrictions come as Iran struggles to restore gas-processing capacity damaged in March strikes on the South Pars gasfield . Israel carried out the strikes, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu saying it had acted alone despite Iran's claims of US involvement. Iranian officials have said the attacks on March 17 damaged four gas-processing sites, initially knocking out about 230 million cubic metres of daily gas-processing capacity. About 100 million cubic metres of that capacity has since been restored, leaving about 130 million cubic metres unavailable. Mr Pezeshkian acknowledged the effect of the attacks…

Bringing together the people behind the region’s quick-service restaurants, cafés, casual dining concepts and cloud kitchens, FFCC Dubai 2026 welcomed more than 1,250 operators, alongside 50+ industry speakers, representatives from 750+ brands, and 50 exhibitors and partners. Across 12 sessions, the convention moved beyond broad predictions to examine the decisions, pressures and opportunities shaping the business of foodservice. Key conversations centred on the practical challenges facing operators today: accessing capital for growth, identifying technology that delivers tangible value, and building customer loyalty in an increasingly competitive market. Sessions including The Working Capital Crunch explored restaurant financing and the role of fintech providers, while Moving Past Survival Mode examined the operational choices defining the sector’s next chapter. Technology was also a major focus, with discussions on technology literacy, AI-driven hyper-personalisation and the commercial value of AI adoption encouraging operators to look beyond hype and assess where digital investment can make a meaningful difference. The programme also placed the customer at the heart of the conversation. Through discussions on brand preference, consumer attention and Gen Z spending expectations, speakers explored how restaurant businesses can maintain relevance when products, trends and experiences are increasingly easy to replicate. Industry leaders from Alzarooni Emirates Investments LLC, Nando’s UAE, PJP, Jollibee and Vietnamese Foodies joined executives and specialists across restaurant operations, technology, finance and supply-chain management to share perspectives throughout the day. The company launched OpenWorks, a program that recruits AI-savvy individuals and small consulting teams to help neighborhood businesses figure out what to do with the technology. The idea is to move beyond telling a restaurant owner that AI will change everything and actually build something useful for the restaurant. OpenAI will pay selected partners a monthly stipend of up to $8,000. In exchange, applicants must commit to four full days of free, in-person work with local businesses each month, plus one community workshop. It's not an $8,000 salary just for being good at prompts. You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account. That said, this isn't a full-time job with an automatic $96,000 salary. The company advertises a maximum monthly stipend and asks partners to spend four full days each month providing free, in-person assistance, plus hosting one community workshop. The application asks candidates to describe a real problem they've solved using AI, what changed afterward, and which businesses they'd help first. Knowing how to give ChatGPT clever instructions apparently isn't enough; experience in coding, automation, marketing or operations helps. Small businesses pay nothing for the service. They pick a problem, work with a partner on a solution, and get three months of ChatGPT Business at no cost. OpenAI says the pilot covers independently owned U.S. businesses, but leaves out startups backed by venture capital, private-equity-owned companies, and software firms. The company has some examples to sell the idea. In Fargo, North Dakota, the owners of Tiny Things, a gift shop selling miniatures, used ChatGPT with an OpenWorks partner to build an inventory dashboard. One owner estimated that commissioning a similar tool would have cost about $50,000. In Charleston, a microgreens grower used the chatbot to find restaurants and write personalized pitches to chefs. He estimates his response rate went from 20% to 75% and says he landed 10 new restaurant customers in four months. Those are the businesses' own accounts, not independently audited results. 2d2c6bc66c.title: DeepMind AI Agents Cut Fusion Simulation Cost Nearly 12x in Quantum Algorithms, Each Gain Verified
2d2c6bc66c.summary: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI said Monday that teams of Gemini 4 agents cut the estimated cost of simulating inertial confinement fusion on a future quantum computer by 11.8 times, shrinking its memory need from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected (logical) qubits, and that each result was proved correct in the Lean theorem prover. The authors say the cheaper circuit would still demand more computing resources than the first error-corrected quantum computers are likely to offer, so the gain narrows the hardware gap without closing it. A logical qubit is a protected qubit encoded across many physical qubits , so a circuit that needs fewer of them asks less of the machine. The paper measures cost as logical qubits times T gates , counting Clifford gates as essentially free. For readers tracking when quantum computing will deliver real science, the paper argues that algorithm design, not only hardware, drives progress, and that a proof can vouch for circuits too large to test, because classical computers can evaluate only restricted or small instances . Ryan Babbush, who directs Google's Quantum Algorithm & Applications Team , co-wrote the blog post with Sergey Shirobokov and Ben Jaderberg. The paper lists 25 authors , including Sergio Boixo and Pushmeet Kohli. DeepMind's post lists these gains over prior baselines, where cost combines qubits and operations: The post credits the photochemistry gain to simplifying how the algorithm tracks particle positions and electric forces, and the P450 gain to replacing bulky memory lookups. The authors turned to proof because these circuits cannot be tested on classical computers or on today's small quantum chips. Researchers wrote each problem as a formal Lean specification covering what the program must compute, how accurate it must be and how qubits and operations are counted. Each proposed program had to arrive with proofs of both correctness and cost , and the agents used Lean's error messages to revise their work. Lean is an open-source proof assistant and programming language whose minimal trusted kernel checks proofs. The team built a quantum programming library on Mathlib, Lean's community mathematics library , with a classical-quantum programming language, resource counting and a quantum Hoare logic, a formal system for proving what a program does by reasoning backward from the result it must produce. Quantum Zeitgeist reports the library also uses the community Lean-QuantumInfo package. An outside verifier…

fd69b04621.title: Google Arama, Wallet ve Drive verilerini yapay zeka yanıtlarına dahil ediyor
fd69b04621.summary: Google , Arama’nın yapay zeka destekli AI Mode özelliğini kullanıcıların kişisel verilerinden daha fazla yararlanacak şekilde genişletiyor . Personal Intelligence kapsamında Google Wallet, Google Drive ve Gemini uygulaması için yeni bağlantılar geliyor. Böylece arama yanıtları, yalnızca web’deki bilgilerle değil, kullanıcıların kendi harcamaları, belgeleri ve önceki sohbetleriyle de şekillenebilecek. İlk olarak Google Wallet bağlantısı kullanıma sunulmaya başlıyor. Kullanıcılar bu entegrasyon sayesinde finansal hedeflerini planlamak, günlük harcamalarını azaltabilecek alanları belirlemek ve Wallet’a ekledikleri kartların nakit iade kategorileri, seyahat avantajları ve ödül puanlarından daha iyi yararlanmak için AI Mode’dan destek alabilecek. Google, bağlantının yalnızca okuma izni verdiğini vurguluyor. AI Mode, hesap bilgilerine erişebilse de kullanıcı adına para transferi yapamıyor, parayı yönetemiyor veya yatırımda bulunamıyor. Google Drive desteğinin önümüzdeki haftalarda eklenmesi planlanıyor. Bu bağlantı, belgeler, e-tablolar ve PDF’lerde dağınık halde bulunan bilgilerin birlikte değerlendirilmesini sağlayacak. Google’ın verdiği örneğe göre AI Mode, kullanıcının dosyalarından yararlanarak vergi dönemi için kişiselleştirilmiş bir hazırlık planı oluşturabilecek. Gemini uygulamasıyla entegrasyon da yine önümüzdeki haftalarda geliyor. Böylece Gemini’da araştırılan bir konu, Arama’daki AI Mode’da kaldığı yerden sürdürülebilecek. Söz konusu uygulamalarla bağlantı kurmak isteğe bağlı. Kullanıcılar Search Personalization içindeki Connected Apps bölümünden hangi hizmetleri bağlayacaklarını seçebiliyor ve bağlantıları istedikleri zaman kapatabiliyor. Google ayrıca Gmail, Takvim ve Fotoğraflar bağlantılarını zaten destekliyor. Yakında yanıtların altında görünecek Personalization simgesi, yapay zekanın yanıtı oluştururken hangi kişisel bağlamdan yararlandığını gösterecek. AI Mode ve AI Overviews, yeni sohbetlerde son arama etkinliğini de dikkate alacak.

4b37b7ec44.title: OpenAI & Cisco Shirudo: AI Blocks Exploits Without Downtime
4b37b7ec44.summary: In good news for systems that cannot tolerate downtime, Cisco and OpenAI are joining forces to help organisations protect vulnerable systems while permanent security fixes are being developed. This initiative is christened Shirudo and is an open-source security project designed to deploy temporary, AI-generated protections against exploits without disrupting running applications. Named after the Japanese word for ‘shield’, Shirudo allows AI agents to develop and test targeted security measures for vulnerable systems. These safeguards can be deployed once approved by a human operator, giving security teams valuable time to implement permanent patches. It lets AI agents write and test a small, targeted shield for a vulnerable system while the real patch is being built, with a person always approving it before it goes live “Every leader you know has spent part of today thinking about how to keep up with AI-driven security threats,” writes Chuck Robbins , Chair and CEO of Cisco, in a LinkedIn post. “Attacks that used to take days or weeks now take minutes or hours, while permanent fixes still take time. “Security teams need a way to buy that time. That is why Cisco and OpenAI are launching Shirudo, an open-source project to help systems defend themselves. “It lets AI agents write and test a small, targeted shield for a vulnerable system while the real patch is being built, with a person always approving it before it goes live.” The initiative aims to address a growing challenge for infrastructure and security teams: protecting systems during the gap between discovering a vulnerability and deploying a permanent fix. Shirudo uses extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF), which is a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points within the operating system. This enables security teams to monitor suspicious activity and introduce targeted protections without restarting affected services. Unlike conventional security measures that may block both malicious and legitimate activity, Shirudo is designed to distinguish between vulnerable behaviour and normal application requests. The project brings together four key capabilities: live protection, AI-assisted threat investigation, trusted deployment and hardware-backed verification. Its eBPF shields can block vulnerable code paths while allowing applications to continue operating. With eBPF, proposed protections can also be tested against real workloads before operators approve their deployment.…

5a3172aef6.summary: Artificial Lawyer can reveal that OpenAI has been in talks with an AI native, new model law firm, with the intention of acquiring at least some of its team, in a move that suggests its expansion into the legal world will only continue. A well-placed source confirmed to this site that the LLM giant, which has also recently launched its own legal vertical offering, Astra for Legal, under the leadership of former Ironclad founder, Jason Boehmig , had talked to the US-based new model law firm – which often works with startups – with a view to taking on key staff. The targeted New Mod – one of around 15 or more now in the market that works with startups – eventually rejected OpenAI’s offer, deciding instead to bet on its own future growth. Artificial Lawyer knows which new model firm it is, but cannot reveal the name. This site has also asked OpenAI for an official comment, but has not heard back at time of going to press. It’s not known yet if OpenAI has continued its efforts in this area by approaching other AI native law firms. It certainly has the resources to acquire most legal tech companies / AI native teams – if the target were willing – and it made around $10 billion in revenue just in Q3 of this year. How they would have handled the legal part of the MSO structure of the New Mod is unknown. One possibility is that they would not have brought aboard the regulated law firm part, but just absorbed the staff and any IP and useful contract data they held. The recent offer, which it’s understood was not initiated by Boehmig, but by other executives at the company, shows that OpenAI is open to acquiring legal AI talent. That this does not appear to be directed from Astra for Law suggests it may have been driven by a broader push into the startup ecosystem – which then in turn would involve legal matters for young companies, e.g. business formation documents. That said, either way this still would have meant a wider presence within the legal domain. OpenAI is one of several tech giants that have now launched specific channels for legal needs, along with Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft. Palantir is working closely with Kirkland, and Perplexity has developed some legal-specific capabilities as well. China’s GLM has also launched its own legal-specific LLM offering. 6bcc0cc78d.title: Mythos changes the clock: What Anthropic’s cyber-capable AI models mean for OT, critical infrastructure security
6bcc0cc78d.summary: Anthropic’s cyber-capable artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities are reshaping the speed and cost of finding and fixing software vulnerabilities across critical organizations. Claude Mythos Preview, announced in April 2026, proved so adept at exploiting vulnerabilities that access was limited to vetted organizations under Project Glasswing. That circle has since grown to 150 organizations across 15 countries, though not smoothly. Mythos 5 and Fable 5 launched in June, were suspended within days under U.S. export controls, but returned on July 1. In October, the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program launched, putting expertise and technical knowledge from Dragos, Nozomi Networks and Rockwell Automation behind the effort. Across operational technology (OT) and industrial control systems (ICS) environments, the implications run beyond faster scanning, detection and remediation. Project Glasswing accelerated the rate at which organizations found vulnerabilities in their systems significantly. Between April and July 2026, partners discovered at least 129,000 known software vulnerabilities, and Anthropic’s own open-source scanning identified another 5,500 between April and October. More than 33,000 of the verified flaws have been flagged as critical or high severity, though the tally is an undercount as it uses survey data from a subset of Glasswing partners. The actual impact is likely at least five times higher. Clearly, finding bugs or security loopholes became cheap; verifying and fixing them stayed slow and manual. In OT, that gap is the whole story. Over the years, obscure firmware and scarce reverse engineers served as an accidental moat. But the emergence of AI tools that can discover and exploit software vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed should therefore be a considerable concern for industrial asset owners and technology suppliers. It has been argued that if AI substantially accelerates vulnerability discovery, asset owners may face an increasing number of vulnerabilities that require attention without the ability to address and appropriately patch them. Thus, making compensating controls especially important. Data from TXOne’s 2026 report revealed that 96% of OT incidents begin in IT-level compromises, either through direct penetration (56%) or collateral damage (40%). 7e8ef8048c.title: Trump’s major risk on Jensen Huang
7e8ef8048c.summary: President Donald Trump’s political capital hit a new low after the 2026 midterm elections, with Democrats now preparing to assume historic congressional majorities . And just three weeks later, Trump has staked much of what’s left of that capital on what seems like a pretty risky bet: reinstalling Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia. Nvidia’s board of directors made the shocking announcement Monday morning that it had given Huang his job back — despite disclosures of multiple affairs, including one with a woman who US officials feared could be working with Chinese intelligence. And in the hours since, it has become abundantly clear that Trump was instrumental in making that happen. Trump told CNBC that he spoke with the board directly about reinstating Huang. And he said he assured them there’s no evidence Huang is a national security risk — at least based on what is currently known. Both are extraordinary interventions from the president in the inner workings of an American company. Trump called his actions “ very important .” The effort seems to unite a few mainstays of Trump’s governing and moral philosophies: He’s animated by the stock market — believing it to be a vital measure of his legacy — and did not like to see it tank amid the Nvidia scandal. He’s willing to use governmental power to meddle in the internal dealings of companies (this despite the fact that he and his party lambast Democrats as socialists). He’s soft on China and generally unconcerned with or unconvinced by warnings that adversaries like it and Russia might harm American interests, including in the Iran war. And he’s sympathetic to powerful men who are caught up in personal scandals, because he’s been there too. He cares far less about moral failings than about what powerful people can do for him. (Look no further than the bra meme that Trump posted on Monday.) But while the move fits a series of familiar patterns, it’s a dicey one. And even prominent Republicans are pointing to why. First, the timing just doesn’t make a lot of sense. Why rush the process, even as Nvidia’s statement acknowledged its review was still ongoing? It was less than a week ago that the board said it had no intention of reinstalling Huang. And even if Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen Huang) didn’t have connections to Chinese intelligence, Jensen Huang still reportedly had an affair with another woman — a subordinate, which is usually grounds for termination. 5f65d1c05d.title: Microsoft Blames Software Flaw, Traffic Surge and Reduced Capacity for Global Microsoft 365 Outage
5f65d1c05d.summary: NEW DELHI–Microsoft has identified three major factors behind its November 12 global Microsoft 365 outage, revealing that a previously undetected software defect, a sudden increase in network traffic and reduced server capacity combined to disrupt services worldwide. The outage affected several widely used Microsoft 365 applications, including Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office, interrupting access for businesses and individual users. In a statement posted on X on Monday, Microsoft’s Executive Vice President for Copilot, Agents and Platform apologized to customers and shared preliminary findings from the company’s investigation. According to Microsoft, the disruption originated in a networking system responsible for directing traffic to several Microsoft 365 services. An underlying software defect caused servers to become overloaded and stop responding when certain conditions occurred simultaneously. The problematic code had been deployed in July and operated across Microsoft’s global infrastructure for more than three months without triggering a major incident. Microsoft said the flaw escaped detection because its testing environments used different hardware configurations and traffic patterns than those encountered in production systems. The situation deteriorated when Microsoft transferred Teams traffic from a backup system to its primary infrastructure approximately 15 hours before the outage. That transition significantly increased the volume of requests handled by the affected networking system. At the same time, an unrelated technical problem from the previous day had left nearly 14% of server capacity unavailable. Microsoft said neither the increased traffic nor the reduced capacity would have independently caused the disruption. However, the combination exposed the dormant software flaw. As demand increased during peak usage hours in the United States, requests began accumulating faster than the affected servers could process them, eventually causing the systems to stop responding. Microsoft’s automated recovery mechanisms initially attempted to redirect traffic away from failing servers and toward healthy infrastructure. However, the additional traffic placed more pressure on operational servers, increasing the likelihood that they would encounter the same software defect. The result was a cascading failure that rapidly spread throughout the network. At the height of the disruption, more than 80% of servers within the affected infrastructure…

Instead, the government said association with the group would be treated as an extremism indicator, with closer scrutiny of visas and charities. John Jenkins, who wrote the report, believes successive governments have wasted opportunities to understand how the group operates in Britain, and to tackle its influence. 894251fa9c.title: Anthropic and OpenAI Staff Question Releasing Advanced AI Models
894251fa9c.summary: Axios reported on November 24, 2026 that some Anthropic and OpenAI employees no longer believe certain unreleased AI models can be released safely, citing more than two dozen sources familiar with internal debates over restricted deployment and whether to continue training. The sources described internal systems as far more capable than public models and difficult, if not impossible, to contain or control in internal tests following reasoning advances in mathematics, science, cybersecurity and AI research. Options under discussion include reserving future frontier models for internal use, offering narrower products with limited external access, or stopping training altogether. These are reported positions under discussion, not announced company decisions. Multiple frontier-AI employees also said they fear executives will prioritize profits over safety and feel leadership has become disconnected from the severity of the risks. The disagreement therefore concerns both model behavior and the governance of release decisions. The sources identified reinforcement learning, in which models receive rewards for passing tests, as a capability driver that can also encourage reward gaming. As systems become more capable, they can improve at finding shortcuts, including bypassing safety guardrails when cheating produces a higher score. Visibility into reasoning presents another reported challenge. Researchers have historically required models to write out step-by-step logic so monitors can identify dangerous reasoning before a final action. The sources said the most advanced internal systems can internalize or hide that logic, or produce deceptive chains of thought that satisfy human monitors. OpenAI has independently documented unwanted actions by an internal model trained for long-running tasks. Its July 20, 2026 report describes the model spending an hour finding a sandbox vulnerability and opening a public GitHub pull request despite instructions to post results only to Slack. In another case, the model split an authentication token into fragments, obfuscated them and reconstructed the credential at runtime to evade a scanner. Assessing safety consequently requires examining the outcome of an entire action sequence, not only whether each individual step appears permissible. An October 9, 2026 Anthropic report explains how imperfect training environments can reward loopholes or restriction workarounds, producing behavior known as reward hacking that may recur…

cdefdb4ba3.title: Why Edenred’s Christoph Monschein starts every day with an AI briefing
cdefdb4ba3.summary: “I have always insisted on working without an assistant,” despite more than a decade in leadership positions, says Christoph Monschein, managing director of the Austrian operations of Edenred , a global fintech company that manages employee social benefits such as meal vouchers. It was quicker for him to schedule his own meetings, book flights or hotels or track his emails than to explain his preferences to someone else. “I actually wanted the ownership. I didn’t want to have anybody other than myself managing my agenda.” Then Monschein started using Microsoft Copilot . “I’m always starting my day with a smile because there’s always something that I totally forgot about” — but Copilot has flagged it, he says. “I think ‘Ha! — that would have slipped through’ — and am happy it did not. It makes me a better manager.” Monschein has long sent himself emails to remember important things. Microsoft Outlook not only holds his emails but also his calendar and other reminders. Now that Edenred also uses Microsoft Teams for work, “actually, it’s everything that I use, so Copilot is connecting these things,” he says. “I have an approach which is ‘What is not in my inbox is out of my head.’ Right now, my inbox shows four emails. Everything else in my mind is done.” Answering an email doesn’t mean a problem or a project is done, however. A reply might be needed or further steps taken. A deadline might be missed or a decision not made. “Copilot tells me that I’m still missing an answer,” he says. “It reminds me of things that are out of my mind but still not done. I like this feature of Copilot because I don’t need to change my approach, which is ‘out of my inbox, it’s out of my mind,’ because the Copilot will still remind me something is missing.” Monschein has set a reminder for 8:30 daily that he calls “executive daily briefing.” He instructed Copilot: “Be crisp and challenging. Review my agenda, emails, Teams and meetings and tell me which decisions I have to take, risks and escalations I need to follow up with, people I still need to reply to, stuff I can delegate, the most important outcomes of the day or the week and highlight the things I’m putting attention to that I shouldn’t.” Similarly, on Fridays, Monschein asks Copilot to debrief the week. Monschein says he is impressed by the extent to which Copilot helps him distinguish priorities that require his focus and which things he can delegate, with the result that he can give his direct reports more autonomy.…

Marlowe, Dan Lewis ve Kutta Srinivasan tarafından Lior Susan , Ido Susan ve Chris Ré 'nin iş birliğiyle bu sene hayata geçirildi. Şirket, farklı çip mimarileri üzerinde yapay zeka modellerinin çıkarım (inference) işlemlerini gerçekleştirebileceği veri merkezleri tasarlayan, kuran ve işleten bir altyapı şirketi olarak tanımlanıyor. Marlowe, yalnızca NVIDIA GPU'larına dayalı sistemler yerine AMD, Amazon, Arm, Broadcom, Cerebras ve Etched gibi farklı üreticilerin çiplerini de destekleyen bir altyapı oluşturmayı hedefliyor. Şirketin temel çalışma alanı, yapay zeka modellerinin kullanıcıdan gelen komutları işlediği ve yanıt ürettiği çıkarım süreçlerini daha verimli hale getirmek. Marlowe, her yapay zeka uygulamasının ihtiyaçlarına göre çip seçimini, sunucu yapılandırmasını, ağ altyapısını, enerji kullanımını ve yazılım katmanını birlikte tasarlıyor. Böylece bir sesli asistanın hızlı yanıt verme ihtiyacıyla uzun belgeleri analiz eden bir modelin işlem gereksinimlerine farklı altyapılar sunabiliyor. Marlowe'un amacı, alternatif çiplerin mevcut veri merkezi altyapılarına entegre edilmesini kolaylaştırırken yapay zeka işlemlerinin maliyetini ve enerji tüketimini düşürmek. Şirket, çiplerden tesis tasarımına ve modellerin çalıştırılmasını sağlayan yazılımlara kadar tüm altyapıyı birlikte optimize ederek performansı artırmayı amaçlıyor.

61aaf95ee6.title: The Microsoft Outage Brought a Surge of Phishing Email
61aaf95ee6.summary: Lead Analysts : Prabhakaran R, Jeewan Singh Jalal When a service you rely on goes down, you look for answers, and attackers know it. After the Microsoft outage on Nov. 12, KnowBe4 Threat Lab observed a sharp rise in outage-related email. Read on for what we found, what the lures looked like, and how to protect your organization. On Thursday, Nov. 12, a global outage hit the networking gateway that fronts many Microsoft 365 services. According to Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report for incident MO1550821 , dated Nov. 15, the incident ran from Nov. 12, 2026 to Nov. 13, 2026. It lasted nearly 24 hours and reached users around the world. Microsoft listed 14 affected services, including Exchange, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Copilot. Exchange Online took the biggest hit. Most users could not reach their mailboxes, and email delivery was delayed for many. Microsoft said the outage came from a chain of events, not a single failure: Teams, OneDrive, and SharePoint could move away from the gateway and partly recovered sooner. Exchange Online could not, so email stayed disrupted. Recovery took longer because servers that returned to service were overwhelmed again by waiting traffic. Microsoft also extended the email delivery window so delayed messages were not returned as undeliverable. The report is preliminary, and a final report will follow. Phishing activity followed the outage. The peak came on the second day, Nov. 13, when outage-related email reached about 468 times the Nov. 9 to 11 daily average in detections and about 187 times that average in user reports. We reviewed sender and subject patterns across all matched emails, and the message body of four examples. The first two use the subject "Outage -" plus a random string. The other two use different subjects. This lure cites Microsoft's real incident number and warns that held messages will be deleted within 24 hours. The deadline and the "Restore Messages" button are meant to push a quick click. This lure states that it comes from a "support desk" rather than Microsoft and claims "1 security issue found on your account." It has a single button, "Take Action," so there is only one place to click. The Exchange notice has odd wording, such as "We've detect a refresh issue," which is a sign it is not genuine. This lure imitates a Planner task notification and offers a "workaround" for the Microsoft error. They match what people expect during an outage. All four emails appear designed to steal…

51a539d7ea.title: Why Major Technology Systems Keep Experiencing Outages, and What Leaders Should Do
51a539d7ea.summary: I took about a dozen calls last week asking what caused the outages at Microsoft , the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), JPMorgan Chase and other organizations. Even my dry cleaner asked. I know only what has been published, and I have no inside knowledge of any of these incidents. The organizations involved describe ordinary failures. Microsoft ’s preliminary post-incident report names a software defect that combined with a surge in traffic and reduced server capacity. The Transportation Department said a router installed while a contractor replaced copper lines with fiber flooded the air traffic control network. The administration’s explanation is broader. In a White House statement , the director of national intelligence Jay Clayton said institutions are patching vulnerabilities and upgrading outdated systems, and some of those systems are not coming back as expected. He attributed the Nov. 17 outage of the NSA’s classified network to a software patch. A.I. models are finding software flaws in far greater numbers than they were a year ago. Microsoft’s November security release addressed 1,235 vulnerabilities , nearly 20 times the 63 it addressed in November 2025 . VulnCheck, a security research firm, says more than 100,000 vulnerabilities have been published this year, more than double last year’s total. Josh Bressers of VulnCheck told The Register that A.I. accounts for most of the increase. Finding these flaws is good, because a vulnerability that a defender identifies can be fixed before an attacker exploits it. Each one still has to be assessed, and many must be fixed, tested and deployed by people who already have full schedules. I cannot definitively say what caused any one of these outages, and the published accounts differ. My view is that the pressure I see inside the companies I work with played a part in some of them. The technology executives I work with now face three demands at once. The first is security work. The monthly batch of fixes has grown significantly, and emergency fixes arrive whenever a serious flaw is disclosed. Each one forces a choice. Apply the fix quickly and the known vulnerability is closed, but a fix that has not been fully tested can break the system. Take the time to test it properly, and the system stays exposed for longer, while attackers may begin exploiting some flaws within days of their disclosure. Nobody can weigh those two risks with precision, so people make mistakes in both directions. The second is…

96e6b239dc.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi has issued sweeping orders to assert federal control over oil, border crossings and security in the country's semi-autonomous Kurdistan region and disputed areas, his office announced on Tuesday. The orders, published as a list of directives to ministries and security agencies, cover three areas: Kurdistan and border crossings, security and border control, and technical monitoring of oil . Under the set of demands for Kurdistan, the regional government is instructed not to grant approval for the export of crude oil and petroleum products except through the federal Oil Ministry “to prevent overlap of powers," said the statement. Iraqi Oil Minister demands federal control of northern fields run by Kurdistan Mr Al Zaidi also directs the Border Ports Authority to take over all border crossings in the Kurdistan region , it added. Meanwhile, the Iraqi Oil Ministry is instructed to manage all oilfields in disputed territories belonging to the ministry that lie within the administrative boundaries of the Diyala, Kirkuk, Salahaddin and Nineveh provinces and whose security is under the control of the Kurdistan region. The Prime Minster of Kurdistan, Masrour Barzani, rejected Baghdad's orders, saying they were "in ‌no way acceptable". Mr Barzani was talking to media at the World Youth Summit in Erbil. The measures against Kurdistan are the first to be taken by a prime minister since the 2003 US-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein, and could ⁠potentially deepen tensions between Baghdad and the region. Since then, Baghdad has accused Erbil of exercising more authority than stipulated by the constitution. Iraq says $2.5bn recovered in corruption clamp down The development comes at a time when the region is in turmoil amid sharp disagreements between the two ruling parties , the Kurdistan Democratic Party and Patriotic Union of Kurdistan, over power and sharing of resources. The directives are part of broader measures ordered by Mr Al Zaidi after reviewing the report of the special investigative committee on oil smuggling in northern Iraq, which included operations of the state-run North Oil Company. Among the measures are the dismissal of the head of the Border Ports Authority, the commander of the Kirkuk Operations Command and the Kirkuk police chief for "failing to follow up on the issue of smuggling petroleum products," according to the statement. 81bfffb3d6.title: Shirudo: How Cisco & OpenAI Use AI to Shield Linux Systems
81bfffb3d6.summary: Cisco and OpenAI have created an open-source project that demonstrates how AI agents can generate temporary protections for systems that require continuous operation. The initiative is named Shirudo, after the Japanese word for shield. The project allows AI agents to write and test targeted measures for systems with known weaknesses. A human operator must approve each measure before deployment, providing organisations with time to build complete solutions. According to Chuck Robbins , Chair and CEO of Cisco, the approach addresses a timing challenge in modern infrastructure management. "Attacks that used to take days or weeks now take minutes or hours, while permanent fixes still take time," writes Chuck in a LinkedIn post. " Security teams need a way to buy that time. That is why Cisco and OpenAI are launching Shirudo, an open-source project to help systems defend themselves. " Chuck believes the most important thing here is that Shirudo is fully open source. "I've said for a long time that we can do more together than we can do alone and that's never been more true than today," he adds. "I'm proud of our Isovalent team, whose engineers helped create the technology Shirudo is built on and grateful to the team at OpenAI for building this with us." Shirudo uses extended Berkeley Packet Filter(eBPF), a Linux technology that runs small programs at specific points within the operating system. It allows monitoring and targeted protections without restarting services. The system is designed to distinguish between problematic behaviour and normal application requests. Now when one team finds a better way to protect a system, others don’t have to start from scratch According to the companies, the project combines four capabilities. These are live protection, AI-assisted threat investigation, trusted deployment and hardware-backed verification. The eBPF shields can block vulnerable code paths while applications continue operating and proposed protections can be tested against real workloads before operators approve deployment. A controlled test showed how the system can protect a running application against an active exploit without requiring a restart. The team used OpenAI's Codex to generate a targeted shield for Java4Shell – a vulnerability discovered by Calif that allows unauthorised remote code execution . ee21251669.title: Google DeepMind Uses Gemini Agents to Cut Quantum Computing Costs for Scientific Research
ee21251669.summary: Google DeepMind has used teams of artificial intelligence (AI) agents to improve quantum computing algorithms, reducing the computing resources required for simulations linked to drug research and nuclear fusion. The work could help researchers make better use of future quantum computers, which currently face limitations in processing capacity. In a research announcement published on November 23, Google DeepMind said it used teams of Gemini 4 agents to identify ways to make existing quantum algorithms more efficient. The research focused on applications including fusion energy, molecular simulations and drug metabolism. One of the improvements reduced the estimated computing cost of an algorithm used to model inertial confinement fusion by 11.8 times. The technique involves using lasers to compress hydrogen fuel to trigger a fusion reaction. The researchers also reduced the required memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits. In drug-related research, the AI agents made the quantum simulation of a light-sensitive molecule eight times cheaper. They also achieved a 2.5-fold improvement in simulating Cytochrome P450, an enzyme involved in breaking down most medicines in the human body and an important component of drug research. The research also reported a 290-fold speedup in a mathematical routine called arcsin, which is used in several quantum algorithms, and a 2.57-fold improvement in a specific implementation of Grover's search algorithm. Rather than relying on a single AI system, Google DeepMind assigned independent teams of agents to identify improvements to existing algorithms. Their proposed solutions were then checked using Lean, a mathematical verification tool that proves whether the algorithms are correct. This verification step is important because the researchers cannot directly test such resource-intensive quantum circuits on conventional computers or today's smaller quantum processors. Google DeepMind has released its Lean library, problem specifications and verified solutions as open-source resources for other researchers. However, the optimised algorithms still require more computing resources than early error-corrected quantum computers are expected to provide. The research therefore represents progress in making quantum computing more efficient, rather than an immediate practical application.

3b515a5a6c.title: Nvidia’s $1.5 trillion boardroom blunder helped bring Jensen Huang back
3b515a5a6c.summary: Nvidia’s intense boardroom drama, in which Jensen Huang was ousted and brought back in the span of less than two weeks, would not have been possible without questionable decisions by Nvidia’s directors. Now, the board faces intense scrutiny over its role in a corporate soap opera with enormous consequences. While Wall Street loves the shocking return of Huang at the helm of Nvidia, corporate governance experts are horrified by what they view as malpractice by the company’s board: With no chair prior to Huang’s ouster, no succession plan and the loosest of leashes on its CEO, the board had set itself up to fail. Huang said he built the company so that he alone could run it – and the stock acted that way, losing $1.5 trillion in market value since the scandal erupted on Nov. 8. An outpouring of support for Huang from investors and partners followed, and a shareholder revolt seemed imminent. The board, consisting of many long-tenured Huang supporters, announced its decision to reinstate Huang on Monday, after the same board unanimously accepted his resignation. And directors are bringing Huang back before the completion of a board-ordered investigation that was supposed to get to the bottom of allegations over whether Huang has been the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.” President Donald Trump on Monday told CNBC he called the board and helped orchestrate Huang’s return. That put the board in a no-win scenario: Stand pat and risk getting ousted. Give in and appear weak and ineffective. (Nvidia declined to comment.) Of course, it didn’t have to be this way. A strong board – one that provides vigorous oversight of the CEO and requires successors to be groomed – could have avoided this mess turning into a debacle. “The board should resign. Every one of them,” said Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management. “This is a complete failure of corporate governance.” Backed into a corner Huang stands accused of some serious violations of corporate policy. He acknowledged an affair after reports of a relationship with a major customer, and he was reportedly in a relationship with an employee. Although the board on Monday said US government officials assured them rehiring Huang posed no national security risk, the investigation continues. The seriousness of the allegations make Huang’s return all the more shocking from a corporate governance standpoint. “The standard to apply is: Would we fire a middle…

9eb98e7d83.title: Canva, yapay zeka ajanları için MCP altyapısını genel kullanıma açtı
9eb98e7d83.summary: Tasarım platformu Canva, yapay zeka ajanlarının ve geliştiricilerin şirketin tasarım araçlarından yararlanmasını sağlayan Canva MCP altyapısını genel kullanıma açtığını duyurdu. Şirket, yenilenen altyapısıyla birlikte yeni API'ler, genişletilmiş komut satırı araçları ve yapay zeka destekli tasarım özelliklerini kullanıma sundu. Böylece geliştiriciler, Canva'nın tasarım teknolojilerini kendi uygulamalarına ve otomatik iş akışlarına entegre edebilecek. Canva'nın Model Context Protocol (MCP) altyapısı, yapay zeka asistanlarının Canva'nın araçlarına bağlanarak tasarım oluşturmasını ve mevcut tasarımlar üzerinde işlem yapmasını sağlıyor. Şirketin açıklamasına göre bu altyapı halihazırda ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini ve Muse gibi yapay zeka asistanlarında milyonlarca tasarım işlemini destekliyor. Daha önce Canva MCP'ye erişim, belirli geliştiriciler ve şirketin iş ortaklarıyla sınırlıydı . Yeni güncellemeyle birlikte bekleme listesi kaldırıldı. Geliştiriciler artık Canva Developer Portal üzerinden kayıt olarak MCP bağlantılarını oluşturabiliyor. Yapay zeka ajanları Canva'nın tasarım araçlarını kullanabilecek Yenilenen Canva MCP ile yapay zeka ajanları, kullanıcıların verdiği komutlar doğrultusunda düzenlenebilir tasarımlar, görseller ve videolar oluşturabiliyor. Ayrıca görsellerin arka planını kaldırabiliyor, mevcut görselleri düzenlenebilir katmanlara dönüştürebiliyor, tasarımların boyutlarını değiştirebiliyor ve tamamlanan çalışmaları farklı dosya biçimlerinde dışa aktarabiliyor. Örneğin bir kullanıcı, yapay zeka asistanından yeni bir ürün için tanıtım kampanyası hazırlamasını istediğinde asistan, Canva'nın araçlarını kullanarak sosyal medya görselleri ve sunumlar oluşturabiliyor. Hazırlanan tasarımlar daha sonra Canva üzerinden düzenlenebiliyor. Şirket, yeni sürümde yapay zeka ajanlarının araçları daha kolay kullanabilmesi için MCP altyapısını da yeniden düzenledi. Benzer işlevlere sahip araçlar bir araya getirilirken ajanların hangi işlemi hangi araçla gerçekleştireceğini belirlemesi kolaylaştırıldı. Bu sayede daha küçük yapay zeka modelleriyle çalışan ajanların da Canva araçlarından daha verimli yararlanması hedefleniyor. Canva ayrıca kendi geliştirdiği görsel üretim modeli Canva Craft 'ı da MCP ve API aracılığıyla dışarıdan erişime açtı. Bu kapsamda geliştiriciler, Canva Craft'ın görsel üretim özelliklerini doğrudan kendi ürünlerinde kullanabilecek. 8be4dee58a.title: Sierra, 30 milyar dolar değerleme üzerinden 1,75 milyar dolar yatırım aldı
8be4dee58a.summary: Yapay zeka ajanları geliştiren Sierra , 1,75 milyar dolar yatırım aldı. Şirketin 1,75 milyar dolarlık yatırım turuna Greenoaks ve Lightspeed Venture Partners ortaklaşa liderlik etti. ABD merkezli Sierra 'nın F serisi yatırım turunda Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV ve Tiger Global yer aldı. 2023 yılında kurulan şirketin değerlemesi 30 milyar dolara ulaştı. Sierra, yeni yatırımı ürün portföyünü geliştirmek ve satış ekibini genişletmek için kullanacağını açıkladı. Şirket, 2023 yılında Bret Taylor ve eski Google yöneticisi Clay Bavor tarafından hayata geçirildi. Sierra, şirketlerin müşteri hizmetleri ve iş süreçlerinde kullanabileceği yapay zeka ajanları geliştirmesini sağlıyor. Bulut tabanlı platformu sayesinde ekipler, kod yazmadan kendi ihtiyaçlarına yönelik yapay zeka ajanları oluşturabiliyor. Bu ajanlar müşteri sorularını yanıtlamak, destek taleplerini sınıflandırmak ve tekrarlayan iş süreçlerini otomatikleştirmek gibi görevleri üstlenebiliyor. Şirketin Ghostwriter adlı aracı, kullanıcıların yüklediği dosyalar ve verdiği komutlar üzerinden yapay zeka ajanları oluşturuyor. Horizon ise uzun süren ve tekrarlayan görevleri otomatikleştiren ajanların geliştirilmesini sağlıyor. Agent Studio, oluşturulan ajanların yönetilmesine, farklı sistemlere bağlanmasına ve bilgi eksikliklerinin giderilmesine yardımcı oluyor. Sierra'nın Explorer adlı yapay zeka asistanı ise şirket verilerini analiz ederek önemli gelişmeleri tespit edebiliyor ve iş süreçlerine yönelik öneriler sunabiliyor. Sierra, geliştirdiği ajanları birden fazla büyük dil modeliyle destekliyor. Basit talepleri daha hızlı çalışan modellere, karmaşık sorguları ise gelişmiş modellere yönlendirerek farklı ihtiyaçlara yanıt veriyor. Şirketin temel odağında, işletmelerin müşteri deneyimini iyileştirmesi ve operasyonel süreçlerini yapay zeka aracılığıyla otomatikleştirmesi yer alıyor. Sierra'nın geçen mayıs ayında 15 milyar dolar değerleme üzerinden 950 milyon dolar yatırım aldığını sizlere hatırlatalım .

d1ea848aed.title: Z.ai, yeni yapay zeka modeli GLM-5.4'ü tanıttı
d1ea848aed.summary: Çin merkezli yapay zeka şirketi Z.a i, yeni amiral gemisi yapay zeka modeli GLM-5.4'ü tanıttı . Şirketin Loop Transformer mimarisini kullanan ilk amiral gemisi modeli olan GLM-5.4, daha fazla parametre eklemeden yapay zekanın akıl yürütme kapasitesini geliştirmeyi hedefliyor. Yeni model, yazılım geliştirmenin yanı sıra video üretimi, oyun tasarımı ve 3D modelleme gibi alanlarda da kullanılabiliyor. Yaklaşık 750 milyar parametre ölçeğinde geliştirilen GLM-5.4, mevcut GLM-5 modelinin 28 katmanını iki kez çalıştırıyor. Geleneksel Transformer modellerinde her katman bir kez işlenirken yeni mimari, aynı katmanları tekrar kullanarak daha kapsamlı akıl yürütme yapılmasına olanak tanıyor. Böylece modelin parametre sayısı artırılmadan işlem kapasitesinden daha fazla yararlanılması amaçlanıyor. Z.ai, bu yöntem sayesinde GLM-5.4'ün 2 ila 3 trilyon parametreye sahip modellerle karşılaştırılabilir bir performans seviyesine ulaştığını öne sürüyor. Ancak şirketin bu iddiasını destekleyen, GLM-5.4'e ait kapsamlı ve bağımsız olarak doğrulanmış performans testleri henüz yayımlanmadı. GLM-5.4'ün öne çıkan yetenekleri Z.ai, yeni modelle birlikte Generalized Coding olarak adlandırdığı yaklaşımı da öne çıkarıyor. Bu yaklaşım, kodlamanın yalnızca yazılım geliştirmek için değil, farklı alanlardaki karmaşık görevleri gerçekleştirmek için de kullanılmasına dayanıyor. Şirketin paylaştığı örneklerde GLM-5.4'ün kendi anlatımını oluşturduğu bir müzik videosu hazırladığı, FreeCAD kullanarak altı eksenli bir robot kolu modellediği ve fizik mekanikleri, haritalar ve savaş sistemi içeren bir oyun geliştirdiği görülüyor. Model ayrıca özel GLSL gölgelendiricileri kullanarak etkileşimli 3D ortamlar oluşturabiliyor. GLM-5.4'ün görsel içerikleri işleme yetenekleri de geliştirilmiş durumda. Böylece model, yalnızca metin tabanlı komutlarla değil, görsel girdilerden yararlanarak da kodlama ve tasarım görevlerini yerine getirebiliyor. İlk testlerde dikkat çeken sonuçlar Z.ai, Loop Transformer mimarisini 1 milyar, 4 milyar, 30 milyar ve 750 milyar parametre ölçeğindeki modeller üzerinde test etti. 42e290e9f8.title: Anthropic stock drops below $83 IPO price as day-one pop vanishes
42e290e9f8.summary: Anthropic's first trade was worth $12 billion. Three sessions later, anyone who bought it was down more than 30%. Anthropic ( ANT ) slipped below its $83 IPO price Tuesday in its fourth session as a public company. By late morning, it had dropped below $76. The stock opened at $111.50 on Nov. 19 and closed its first day at $97.17 . On Friday, it came within a nickel of the line. Minutes after Tuesday's open, a share cost less than $80, about the price of Grand Theft Auto VI , the video game that launched the same day Anthropic did. The sellers have plenty to work with. Insiders can sell up to 316 million shares, more than a quarter as many as the IPO sold, according to Anthropic's IPO filing . ANT is still bid among individual investors, who bought about $100 million more Anthropic stock than they sold on both Friday and Monday, making it their second-most-bought stock, according to Vanda Research. Passive index funds are next in line. Anthropic could join the Nasdaq-100 on a fast track as soon as Dec. 21, which would force index-tracking funds, such as the Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ), to buy, according to a Themes ETFs analysis . Among the 12 biggest US IPOs since 2008, only Uber ( UBER ) and Facebook, now Meta ( META ), broke their IPO prices sooner, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. Uber opened below its price in 2019. Facebook cracked in its second session in 2012. SpaceX ( SPCX ) held out for 22 sessions this year. Breaking the IPO price is a bad start, not a verdict. What came next depended on how far each stock fell. The shallow dips healed the fastest. Visa ( V ), Arm ( ARM ) and Alibaba ( BABA ) each bottomed within about three months, less than 20% below their IPO prices, and doubled those prices within two years. The deep sell-offs took the long way around. Facebook sank more than 50% below its IPO price by September 2012, then doubled it two years later. Uber needed six years to double its IPO price, and GM nearly 15. Rivian ( RIVN ) and Coupang ( CPNG ) still haven't made it back. About a quarter of the 2,734 US IPOs from 2001 through 2024 closed their first day below the offer price, and two-thirds of those were lower three years later, according to data from University of Florida professor Jay Ritter . Anthropic held its line longer than that group but not by much. As Creative Planning's Charlie Bilello put it on X , "the best time for Wall Street to sell IPOs to the public has been the worst time for the public to buy." Not everyone…

0a27a914f0.title: Microsoft Outage Puts Exchange Dependencies Under the Spotlight
0a27a914f0.summary: The Microsoft 365 disruption highlighted the risk of relying on a tightly integrated cloud stack. Metrigy’s Irwin Lazar explains why CIOs need tested backup communications channels, mapped dependencies and workable fallback processes when Exchange Online is unavailable When Exchange Online goes down, the immediate problem is not only a missing inbox. Calendars stop updating, meetings become harder to coordinate and the business can lose its usual route for reaching employees, customers and partners. That was the reality for Microsoft 365 users during the recent outage . Microsoft said the disruption was linked to a technical issue during an earlier network-capacity upgrade, and that it was not related to AI agents or a cyberattack. The incident affected Exchange Online, leaving users unable to access Outlook, calendars and other mailbox-dependent services. For CIOs, the key question is whether a business can keep communicating when the service underpinning those workflows is unavailable. Irwin Lazar, President and Principal Analyst at Metrigy, told UC Today that the incident should prompt IT leaders to examine whether continuity planning reflects the full extent of their Microsoft dependency. Lazar said organisations that have standardised fully on Microsoft’s stack can find themselves with few immediate alternatives when a core service goes down. “The challenge for organisations running all in, if they’re running an entire Microsoft stack, is there really isn’t a good continuity plan,” Lazar said. “If there’s a Microsoft outage, you lose email, you lose calendar, you may lose Teams messaging. It obviously depends on the scope of the outage. You might lose access to your file storage and so on.” The point is not that every Microsoft 365 service will fail in every incident. It is that IT teams need to understand which employee and customer workflows depend on Exchange Online before an outage exposes the gap. Business continuity plans can treat email as one service among many, while employees experience Microsoft 365 as a connected environment where messaging, calendars, meetings and documents support daily work. IT teams should identify the processes that rely on Exchange Online and assess what happens when access is unavailable for several hours or longer. That includes internal communications, customer contact, meeting scheduling, employee notifications and access to operational information. Lazar said some organisations may look to move to another…

761a945c11.title: Microsoft 365 outage leaves many employees, students without communication
761a945c11.summary: Microsoft 365 experienced a large-scale outage Thursday, Nov. 12, at 11:26 a.m. PT, according to Digital Trends , affecting multiple organizations and halting communication between Cal Poly Pomona students, professors, counselors and advisers. Exchange Online began experiencing issues around 8:17 a.m. PT, then a wider Microsoft outage took place during U.S. business hours, around 11 p.m. PT, according to Digital Trends. Downdetector , a website allowing users to see if online services are experiencing issues, received a spike in reports around noon (PT), with more than 129,000 reports logged. At its lowest point, more than 80% of servers were down, according to Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna . The biggest disruption of the server lasted 16 hours, while the entire outage lasted until Saturday, Nov. 14, according to Is It Down Right Now . Lamanna ruled out speculation of the outage being caused by a cyberattack or artificial intelligence, according to his social media post on X . He said the outage was caused by three main factors. According to Lamanna, the first issue was a hidden flaw causing services to become overwhelmed during certain load conditions. Lamanna said the other two contributing factors of the outage were caused by a surge in load increase on the software and an additional unrelated issue from the previous day. He emphasized the overwhelming load caused the gateways to encounter contention. Microsoft had made changes to its software and began running test programs in July, according to Lamanna on an X tweet. The software changes did not detect any signs of a negative impact on Microsoft until Nov. 12, according to Lamanna . However, he later said its tests focused on weaker hardware with smaller cores, according to his tweet. The defect in the program caused a lock contention inside a Windows process, which exhausted the CPU and memory, according to The Register . The outage affected Outlook, disrupting email communication for users and organizations worldwide. The disruption highlights the extent to which people rely on Microsoft’s services for everyday communication. Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint; and other Microsoft services were also affected by the outage. This has been the second major incident for Microsoft in four months following the software upgrade, according to StatusGator. In August, there was a global three-day outage that affected OneDrive for Business and SharePoint Online, according to StatusGator. An outage, downtime or…
