0720eff473.title: Why a plan to restrict the Iran war could shut down the government before Christmas
0720eff473.summary: Lawmakers have until Dec. 11 to pass a funding bill, with potential impacts on air travel, government services, and military operations in Iran. Lawmakers have until Dec. 11 to pass a funding bill, with potential impacts on air travel, government services, and military operations in Iran. Lawmakers are racing to pass a funding bill before Dec. 11 to prevent a government shutdown that could disrupt air travel, delay government services, and impact military operations in Iran. The federal government is funded until Dec. 11, but if lawmakers fail to reach an agreement by then, Americans could face a wide range of consequences. Air travel could be disrupted if air traffic controllers experience delays in receiving their pay. Families relying on government services, such as SNAP benefits and federal housing programs, could also face delays depending on the length and scope of a potential shutdown. The debate over the spending bill includes a push by some Democrats to restrict funding for military operations in Iran. Earlier this month, Democratic Sens. Michael Bennet , Tammy Duckworth, and Chris Van Hollen joined Independent Sen. Bernie Sanders in demanding these restrictions as part of any short-term funding agreement. California Rep. Ro Khanna has also signaled his support for a similar resolution. "The American people want us to fight to bring down prices. The biggest way to bring down prices is to end this war in Iran. We need to stop funding going for more offensive military operations in Iran," Khanna said. At least one Republican says limiting President Donald Trump's military power in Iran could be more dangerous than a shutdown. Rep. Robert Aderholt, R-Alabama , said he would not want to restrict the president's authority if nuclear weapons were involved, even at the risk of a government shutdown. "If they get nuclear weapons, you won't be worrying about a shutdown," Aderholt told Hearst Television on Nov. 12. He stressed that he was not advocating for a shutdown. Congress has limited time to act before funding expires. The Senate has just 10 working days left, while the House has eight, to reach an agreement and avoid another possible shutdown. 6d905aab66.title: Louis Theroux's documentary on Israeli settlers wins International Emmy
6d905aab66.summary: British filmmaker Louis Theroux's work examining the Israeli settler movement in the occupied West Bank and its ambitions to occupy Gaza has won the best documentary prize at the 2026 International Emmy Awards. The production Louis Theroux: The Settlers is one of three programmes exploring Middle Eastern affairs that received accolades at the 54th awards ceremony, held in New York on Monday. ITV's Breaking Ranks: Inside Israel’s War , featuring testimony from Israeli soldiers who served in Gaza, won the current affairs award. The BBC's Prisoner 951 , a drama about the detention of British-Iranian charity worker Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe, won best television movie or mini-series. Produced by Mindhouse Productions for the BBC and released in April last year, The Settlers follows Theroux as he travels across the occupied West Bank, meeting members of the religious-nationalist settler movement and Palestinians affected by their activities. The documentary marks Theroux ’s return to a subject he explored in his 2011 film The Ultra Zionists . In the intervening 14 years, the settler movement has gained considerable political influence, with prominent supporters of settlement expansion occupying senior positions in the Israeli government. Among the documentary's central figures is Daniella Weiss, a veteran leader of the settler movement who openly discusses her ambitions to establish Israeli settlements in Gaza. Theroux also meets Palestinians facing displacement and Israeli activists opposed to settlement expansion. Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank are considered illegal under international law, a position disputed by Israel. The International Emmys also recognised reporting on Israeli military conduct in Gaza through Breaking Ranks: Inside Israel’s War . Directed by British-Iranian filmmaker Ben Zand and broadcast last November, the documentary features first-hand accounts from Israeli soldiers about their military operations in Gaza. Their testimony includes allegations of gross military misconduct, including the killing of Palestinian civilians and the use of Palestinians as human shields. Another British production examining events in the region, Prisoner 951 recounts Zaghari-Ratcliffe ’s six-year detention in Iran between 2016 and 2022 and her husband Richard Ratcliffe’s campaign to secure her release. 301e6eb9c3.title: Iran lashes female singer and her team 74 times each over 'vulgar' concert with no audience
301e6eb9c3.summary: An Iranian singer and four members of her team were severely flogged by authorities on Monday, as part of a court sentence that reignited international criticism over Iran’s punishment of artistic activity and curbs on women’s freedoms. Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, and her colleagues each received 74 lashes in the city of Qom, her lawyer Mostafa Nili told the Emtedad news outlet. Ms Ahmadi, along with Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amir-Ali Pirnia, and Mohsen Lashkari, reported to the sentence enforcement unit of the Qom prosecutor’s office where the sentences were carried out, Emtedad quoted Mr Nili as saying. Iranian singer Shervin Hajipour sentenced over Mahsa Amini protests A court in Qom convicted the performers in June on charges of “hurting public decency” by publishing “vulgar and immoral content in cyberspace” in connection with a concert performed without an audience and broadcast online in December 2024. Ahmadi and eight members of her production team were sentenced to 74 lashes each and barred from leaving the country or performing artistic activities for two years. Their appeals were thrown out in September when an appeals court branch chief claimed evidence and arguments presented by lawyers were “insufficient”. It remains unclear if or when the other individuals’ sentences will be carried out. In the video, which has been viewed 3.2 million times on YouTube, Ahmadi appears without a hijab, which Iranian law requires women to wear in public. She also sings alone, which Iranian authorities have effectively banned women from doing since the 1979 revolution that brought the current clerical leadership to power. In 2018, in an interview with female vocalist Sepideh Jandaghi, the US-based Centre for Human Rights in Iran said women in Iran were theoretically allowed to sing publicly in a choir or solo for female-only audiences, but even then faced major logistical and financial difficulties in organising concerts. Following the confirmation that the flogging sentences had been carried out, Dadban, a group of volunteer lawyers outside Iran, said that lashes were not only a form of corporal punishment but also a form of torture and were unjustifiable on any criminal charge. “The intentional infliction of physical pain and suffering upon an individual through state-sanctioned beatings constitutes cruel and inhuman treatment and, under international human rights standards, amounts to torture,” the group said in a statement published on social media. b62a5e5f94.title: UN warns Black Sea drone attacks threaten food exports as Russia-Ukraine war widens
b62a5e5f94.summary: The UN has warned Security Council members that drone attacks on commercial ships in the Black Sea are threatening food exports , as the war between Russia and Ukraine spreads. 7614bb30ce.title: AI Innovation Institute Partners with OpenAI to Delve into the Science of Human-AI Creativity
7614bb30ce.summary: In a groundbreaking initiative, Stony Brook University’s AI Innovation Institute partnered with OpenAI to study how working with artificial intelligence (AI) impacts human creativity. Building such scientific evidence is crucial to designing the future of education and workforce development. The research, led by postdoctoral researcher Babak Hemmatian and AI Innovation Institute Director Lav Varshney, drew the attention of Ronnie Chatterji, OpenAI’s chief economist, and Rachel Brown, former economic strategist at OpenAI. Through the partnership, OpenAI researchers gave insights on study design, provisioned frontier AI resource access to Stony Brook students in an equitable manner, and offered significant credits for the research team to perform AI-driven data analysis. “With AI advancing rapidly in industry, it is important for Stony Brook to remain at the frontier through direct engagement with leading companies,” said Varshney. “As part of this global AI ecosystem, we are developing a scientific basis for how AI can most effectively uplift human creativity, which is poised to be the most important question for teaching and learning in our age, and a critical factor in how AI is best deployed in numerous societal contexts.” Sharing the research premise, Hemmatian said, “We wanted to study how working with AI in a collaborative context changes the quality and originality of ideas we come up with. Where is AI’s place in the creative process? Is it from the conversation, from the ideas the machine contributes, or from something the person does better because the machine is there?” Combining cutting-edge technology and rigorous empirical design, Stony Brook University and OpenAI are setting the stage for a new era of educational research — one that moves beyond mere anecdote and speculation to establish scientific foundations for how humans and artificial intelligence can best think, learn, and create together — focused especially on the human side of the equation.

Axios said an Anthropic mathematician used an unreleased version of Claude to present a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, while an unreleased OpenAI model helped produce proofs for hundreds of math problems. An Anthropic spokesperson told Axios that keeping a model internal does not make it safe, and that the company may slow down or hold back releases even when it is costly. 335c81d7eb.title: 290 times speedup: Google DeepMind finds faster way to run quantum algorithms
335c81d7eb.summary: Google's DeepMind and Quantum AI labs used teams of AI agents to write quantum algorithms and correct them in a bid to reduce the costs of quantum computations. The agents were powered by Google's latest AI, Gemini 4, and wrote quantum algorithms for a range of problems ranging from fusion energy to drug discovery. Thanks to their superior computational capabilities, quantum computers are considered the future of computing. Using quantum bits, or qubits, to store information, quantum computers can complete in minutes what even the fastest supercomputers take years to compute. This is why there are high hopes that quantum computers will help us solve for problems like climate change, clean energy, material research, and drug discovery. Estimates, however, suggest that to do so, even the best quantum algorithms will require quantum computers with qubit numbers larger than what we might end up building in the near future. For these quantum computers to be useful, they would need algorithms that are smaller and much more efficient. This is where Google turned to its AI agents. Google's DeepMind team divided target tasks between different AI agents, each assigned to do the same thing - reduce the number of qubits used, use fewer operations to arrive at the result, or use a combination of both. Every four hours, the AI agents would sync up in a digital conference and share notes on what they had learned in an open notebook that other agents could access. This was better because ideas were shared among teams and approaches could be discussed and debated to find more efficient methods. Since quantum algorithms themselves are massive and cannot be run on a classical computer, the AI agents used Lean, a formal theorem prover, which also checks the steps of every proof. An algorithm was accepted into the open notebook only if it arrived at the right answer and also listed the costs of its running. The team used a proxy metric of spacetime to compute costs. This was arrived at by multiplying the peak number of logical qubits needed by the algorithm by the number of T gates it runs. In a fault-tolerant quantum computer, a T gate keeps on checking for errors from time to time and prevents them from accumulating, The high savings in computation came from arcsin, the routine used to load numbers into a quantum state and used across quantum algorithms. f758e34deb.title: ‘Code Red means that this is the highest priority work’: Microsoft
f758e34deb.summary: Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” to change how it prevents and handles major outages, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing internal memos. The Microsoft Code Red follows the global outage of 12 to 13 November. It knocked out Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams and Copilot for about 24 hours. Jaspreet Singh broke the story in a Reuters exclusive . Jason Henderson, president of M365 Core, called it the most customer-impacting incident in Exchange Online’s history. Never before had so many customers gone without email for so long, he told staff in a memo on Friday. The outage hit governments from Australia and Japan to the US, delayed trading firms, and disrupted airline communications. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson wrote, according to Reuters. Amanda Silver oversees M365 Core and Work IQ as a corporate vice-president. She described the response in a separate memo on Monday. Engineers worked through a “fog of war”, she wrote. Responders sent more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats. Diagnostic data sat in separate internal tracking systems. As a result, the team struggled to keep one shared picture of its theories and decisions, Silver wrote. Charles Lamanna is Microsoft’s executive vice-president for Copilot, Agents and Platform. He told a Code Red review that the failed part had seen “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures”, according to Silver’s memo. Microsoft has blamed a dormant July defect in Windows for the outage, a scalability bug that went undetected for months. Chief executive Satya Nadella apologised publicly. Microsoft says cyber activity and AI agents played no part. Silver set out five workstreams under the Code Red, covering load shedding, splitting traffic by region, and faster recovery. Microsoft wants to resolve future incidents worldwide within an hour. It also plans to use AI agents to help engineers read system health data faster. Henderson will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team, plus weekly reviews. Substrate runs the engineering behind Microsoft 365’s core services. A Microsoft spokesperson told Reuters that its teams keep working around the clock to apply the lessons learned. Earlier this month, Henderson wrote that urgent patches to M365 Core services took too long to reach users worldwide. In one recent incident, an urgent fix took five to six days. For the most urgent security issues, he wants an hour from detection to safe worldwide deployment.…

0717649085.title: Microsoft declares ‘code red’ for M365 service health after global outage
0717649085.summary: After a multi-day Microsoft 365 disruption, the company wants future worldwide incidents mitigated within an hour Tue 24 Nov 2026 · 11:21 EST · 3 min read Microsoft has declared a “code red” for Microsoft 365 service health. The company has also set a new target: any future worldwide incident should be mitigated within an hour. The trouble started on November 12, 2026, at around 16:17 UTC. At its peak, more than 80% of Microsoft’s North American gateway servers stopped responding. The damage spread quickly to the services companies lean on every day. Exchange Online and Teams were both affected, which meant email and internal chat stumbled at the same moment. Customer impact ended by 11:10 ET on November 13. Microsoft reached full service restoration by November 14. The root cause was not a cyberattack. Microsoft explicitly ruled out malicious activity, and it also ruled out any AI-related failure. Instead, the culprit was a latent defect in the networking gateway servers. It arrived with a code update shipped in July 2026 and sat dormant for months. The flaw involved lock contention in gateway processes. In software terms, multiple processes competed for the same resource. Under heavy enough load, that competition turned into a traffic jam. The gaps were tied to older hardware, where the defect went undetected before rollout. The bug needed a trigger, and it got a combination of them. A failover in Teams traffic pushed extra load onto the gateways. At the same time, maintenance issues had left 14% of servers offline. One piece of good news: Microsoft says no email data was lost. The picture was messier for some consumer users. Certain messages were delayed long enough that they expired before they could be delivered. Microsoft published its post-incident report around November 20-21. The report included an apology and laid out 13 planned fixes. Those fixes focus on improving monitoring and strengthening resilience against future outages. Microsoft serves more than 450 million paid commercial subscriptions. The outage touched users across multiple sectors and spanned dozens of countries. Businesses and governments alike depend on these tools for daily operations. 52577a2eb1.title: Global Microsoft outage affects university students
52577a2eb1.summary: Several Microsoft services underwent a global outage on Nov. 12, with access returning for most the next day. Office apps, OneDrive, Teams and Copilot were among the services impacted. Hospitals, schools, businesses and other essential services were strongly affected by the system being down. Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna posted on X the following Monday, apologizing to customers and elaborating on the causes of the outage. He explained that a dormant defect in the system that was intended to be a fix became overwhelmed. “Taken together, the increased load and the reduced server capacity, caused the network gateway to encounter the latent bug from July,” said Lamanna in the post. “This caused requests to build up until servers ultimately stopped responding. This occurred during the peak window of traffic in the United States.” With accumulating service traffic from more people waiting, the services became unresponsive even after they went online again. Brandon Horton, a senior in cybersecurity, was one of the university students unable to access Microsoft Outlook and other applications for a day. Horton said the outage was frustrating because university systems rely heavily on Microsoft, leaving students without access to Word and email during the outage. “Microsoft is a huge company, people rely on their products for a lot of their services and it also is kind of in the name Office 365, advertises it being available 365 days a year,” said Horton. “For the most part there’s always alternatives, things that could be used so that you’re not relying solely on Microsoft products. However it is also built into many of these softwares’ availability allowances that they allow or expect a 99% uptime and they leave that 1% open to one-offs like this.” Uptime represents the amount of time annually that a service is available and functional, providing a golden standard of reliability if a system was available 99.99% of the time.

248bee37d1.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after 24-hour global outage exposes major engineering flaws
248bee37d1.summary: Microsoft plans to deploy AI agents to accelerate diagnostics and service recovery Dubai: Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” drive to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after a 24-hour outage exposed shortcomings in its engineering systems and crisis response, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters. The Nov. 12-13 outage hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms and disrupted airline communications, fuelling broader concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure. Microsoft said the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents. Microsoft blamed the outage on an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July. CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologized for the disruption. The Code Red signified the most severe and urgent alert to address weaknesses in Microsoft’s engineering and operational practices after the outage disrupted Exchange Online, its cloud-based email service, as well as Outlook, Teams, its Copilot AI assistant and other Microsoft 365 products. It was the most customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online, M365 Core President Jason Henderson said in a memo to staff on Friday. Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, he said. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson added. Amanda Silver, Microsoft’s corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, the company’s workplace intelligence platform for AI agents, said in a separate memo on Monday that engineers had to work through a “fog of war” as the outage unfolded. Despite deploying top engineering personnel, responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats and struggled to maintain a cohesive picture of hypotheses and decisions because diagnostic data was scattered across fragmented internal tracking systems, Silver said. Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures,” according to Silver’s memo. “Our work doesn’t end when service is restored. Our teams keep working around the clock to quickly implement any lessons learned, and our leadership makes sure this is our top priority,” a company spokesperson told Reuters when contacted about the memos. 0e0d7a5512.summary: OpenAI has launched OpenWorks, a new initiative aimed at helping independently owned small businesses integrate AI into their daily operations through free, hands-on assistance from local AI experts. The ChatGPT maker announced the initiative on Nov. 23. The initiative is being introduced as a pilot program across 20 U.S. communities, including New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Atlanta, Houston, Austin and Seattle. OpenAI said the program would build a nationwide network of OpenWorks Partners who would work directly with businesses on projects selected by the owners themselves. Under the program, participating businesses will receive one-on-one assistance, practical training and three months of ChatGPT Business access at no cost. The initiative is open to independently owned restaurants, retail outlets, service firms and manufacturers. However, software and software-as-a-service (SaaS) companies, venture-backed businesses and private equity-owned firms are excluded. OpenAI is also recruiting technically skilled individuals, small teams and AI consultancies to become OpenWorks Partners. Selected participants will receive tools, training resources and a monthly stipend of up to $8,000. Their responsibilities include working with local businesses for several days each month, organizing community workshops and helping employees develop the skills to use AI independently. The collaboration aimed to train around 150 SBDC advisers, who were expected to extend the training to at least 1,000 small businesses through customized workshops. With OpenWorks, however, OpenAI is taking a more direct approach by recruiting and paying its own local experts. OpenAI has highlighted four businesses that have already benefited from the initiative. OpenAI cited the example of Tiny Things, a miniature gift shop in Fargo, North Dakota, owned by Jackie and Jordaan Maahs. b429903da1.summary: By Jennifer Saibil – Nov 24, 2026 at 12:23PM EST 10 stocks we like better than Anthropic › Anthropic ( ANT -8.12% ) made history last week as the largest initial public offering (IPO) ever, raising $81 billion. Companies that go public do so to raise money for specific purposes — usually to fund growth. Anthropic's stated goals for the money it raised were similar to the usual, with an artificial intelligence (AI) twist: Beyond covering its needs for working capital, it plans to lease compute and build infrastructure. If you're bullish on AI but not ready to invest in a young, unprofitable company that has just gone public , you can get exposure to Anthropic’s growth potential by investing in the companies that are set to benefit from the data center build-out it will require. Here are some of them. Anthropic has a five-year deal with Broadcom ( AVGO -3.31% ) for custom AI accelerators worth $161.2 billion. Alphabet ( GOOG -0.92% ) ( GOOGL -1.04% ) is included as well because the chips in question are its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), which Broadcom designs, and Alphabet will lease them to Anthropic. TPUs aren't as versatile as graphics processing units (GPUs), but they don't have to be. They are application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) that are constructed for a much narrower range of workloads, but because of that, they offer a cheaper solution for what they do well. In September, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said that his company expects Anthropic to become its largest custom-chip customer in 2027, and that Broadcom has line of sight to sales of 19 gigawatts of power, in collaboration with Alphabet. He also said that Anthropic would remain its top customer in 2028. On top of that, following a similar model to the one Nvidia ( NVDA -6.97% ) has repeatedly used — and which has been described as “circular financing” — Broadcom has loaned Anthropic $42 billion via a purchase of convertible notes. Alphabet has a $40 billion equity stake in Anthropic, and it also has a partnership with the company that buys its compute power. It may have commitments as high as $200 billion, according to reports. It's not just Google. Anthropic has agreements with multiple companies for compute power, including Amazon ( AMZN -1.18% ) , with which it has commitments for $110 billion in compute capacity. Work can start in either product, Microsoft said, with Copilot drawing in SAP context or Joule drawing in Microsoft 365 context. He described Fabric IQ as the data-side counterpart to Work IQ. Employees can already reach SAP business context from Microsoft Teams through Joule Work, SAP says, and developers in Copilot Studio can add SAP agents to wider workflows. SAP’s customer example is Nestlé, which uses Joule Assistants for accounts receivable workflows. The November 12-13 failure affected governments, businesses and transportation systems while exposing problems not only with the technology behind Microsoft's services but with the company's ability to coordinate its response. Microsoft is now aiming to resolve future worldwide incidents within an hour and plans changes designed to contain failures more quickly and give engineers a clearer view of problems as they unfold. The initiative represents Microsoft's highest level of urgency for addressing weaknesses revealed by the outage, according to internal company memos reviewed by Reuters. Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 products were affected, and M365 Core President Jason Henderson described the event internally as the most disruptive incident for customers in Exchange Online's history. Microsoft attributed the breakdown to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July. The company said the outage was not caused by a cyberattack or AI agents, while CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologized for the disruption. Newsweek has reached out to Microsoft for additional comment. In this case, Code Red refers to an internal Microsoft mobilization reserved for an exceptionally serious operational problem. The designation puts outage-related work at the top of the engineering organization's priorities as Microsoft examines the technical failure and deficiencies in how the incident was managed. Henderson told employees that the designation made the response the team's "highest priority work," according to Reuters. He said a broader review had examined organizational and structural problems that allowed the failure to have such a significant effect on customers. Anish Agarwal, a computer science professor at Columbia University who teaches site reliability and AI, told Newsweek that, in practical terms, such a declaration means other engineering priorities can be put aside. "A Code Red means that engineering projects that are unrelated to the priority goal are frozen and all available teams are dedicated to working on it," Agarwal said. 47b588647a.title: Google DeepMind’s 544-Prompt HFE Test Exposes LLM Consistency Gaps
47b588647a.summary: Google DeepMind on November 24, 2026 launched Humanity’s First Exam on Kaggle, a benchmark of 544 elementary text and image prompts designed to test whether large language models answer routine questions consistently, not just correctly once. The accompanying technical report evaluated 18 frontier and fast-tier models. Its primary measure, family pass^4, estimates the probability that all 16 sampled attempts across four related prompts are correct; family pass@4 instead asks whether at least one of those attempts succeeds. The report ranks GPT-6.2 Astra first at 92.4% family pass^4, followed by GPT-6.2 Sol at 86.9% and Gemini 4 Neon at 85.8%, although all three reached 100% family pass@4. The report calls the difference the Family Reliability Gap: 7.6, 13.1 and 14.2 percentage points, respectively. That difference matters for automated work in which an occasional correct answer is insufficient. The 544 prompts form 136 families, each containing a seed and three controlled variants that preserve the underlying task while changing entities, clause order or visual attributes. The 20 subcategories include object counting, color identification, spatial reasoning, arithmetic, constraint satisfaction and false-premise verification. Of the total, 316 prompts combine text and images, while 228 are text-only. One public example asks for the colors, in order, of the third letter of each word in a neon sign. The reference answer is green, yellow, white, blue, blue. Such tasks are deliberately easy to explain, while their variants test whether a correct answer depends on a particular phrasing or image. Researchers evaluated the models zero-shot in a single turn without external tools, drawing six independent answers per prompt and grading the visible final answer with a deterministic Gemini 3.1 Pro judge. The analysis found that among the top 12 models, 61% to 85% of families with any failed rollout had just one problematic prompt while the other three were solved on all six runs. The report’s failure analysis attributes 73% of wrong-answer rollouts to visual perception, including 31% involving position, direction or paths in images and 23% involving object counting. Among the top nine models, family pass^4 ranged from 83% to 97% on text-only families but fell to 64% to 89% on multimodal families. The report’s reasoning-effort tests show that moving Gemini 4 Carbon from low to high effort raised family pass^4 by 17.4 percentage points overall, with a 42.4-point gain…

4530af1ba6.summary: Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs. The models’ written reasoning and code suggest they draw on math, physics, chemistry, and biological knowledge to reason about protein shapes and interactions with other molecules. In a preprint titled GPT‑6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models , we show that our GPT‑6 family of models has intrinsic capabilities for designing new proteins: the models can design new protein structures and sequences without relying on specialized biology models, using only reasoning and general-purpose coding tools. Proteins do much of the work in living cells. They drive the chemical reactions that sustain life, carry oxygen through the blood, and defend the body against infection. Incorrectly shaped proteins can also cause disease and dysfunction. Proteins are made from chains of chemical building blocks called amino acids. The order, or sequence, of these amino acids helps determine how a protein folds into a three-dimensional shape, which in turn influences what it does. Scientists often start with a clear idea of what they want a protein to do. They might want it to block a signal that helps cancer cells evade the immune system or to help capture carbon dioxide from the air. The challenge is to work out what three-dimensional structure would enable the protein to do its job and which amino acid sequence would give it that structure. Specialized biology models capable of generating three-dimensional protein structures and sequences have made this work more practical. Using and coordinating these specialized models requires substantial expertise. Each accepts particular kinds of inputs and constraints, and these models cannot easily accept new kinds of information without changes to their software or additional training. Newly public stocks face different pressures than their established counterparts. Those pressures often push the stock price high on the first trading day and lower in the days and weeks that follow. Highly anticipated IPOs generate investor excitement. That can drive demand for the stock among a range of investors, including those seeking quick gains and trend followers who haven't read the prospectus. The excitement tends to peak on IPO day, encouraging some investors to buy at almost any price. When the excitement winds down, demand tends to soften. Short-term investors may be in and out of the stock on the first day, while trend followers can lose their conviction quickly as soon as the stock price falters. As time passes, new information, market conditions, and insider liquidations can foster additional share-price declines. Here's why a stock falls below its IPO price. The IPO prospectus is the official disclosure document for the offering, and usually remains the primary information source for several weeks. Additionally, the regulatory body FINRA generally requires underwriters to prohibit their analysts from publishing research reports for at least 10 days after the IPO. 7e27d9ac81.summary: A quantum calculation used to model laser-driven fusion could require 4,338 error-corrected qubits, down from 5,650 in an earlier design, according to researchers at Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI . Teams of Gemini 4 Carbon agents found a way to reduce both the memory needed for the calculation and the number of operations it would take, bringing the combined resource estimate down by a factor of 11.8. The collaboration, described in the preprint Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI , covered five problems. They ranged from routines used in quantum search and arithmetic to simulations in fusion, photochemistry, and drug metabolism. For the scientific simulations, the researchers compared designs using a cost measure that combines the number of error-corrected qubits with the count of a particular quantum operation. The researchers started by writing specifications that defined what each program had to do and how its computing cost would be counted. The agents then proposed circuits and produced mathematical proofs that their designs met those requirements. Lean checked the proofs, while a separate verification step confirmed that each submitted result held against the original specification. The agents also shared verified solutions and unsuccessful ideas through a wiki. They discussed proposals at scheduled virtual meetings, where other teams could pick them up. The final photochemistry circuit, for example, combined ideas from three agent teams. The largest single improvement started as a proposal from one team that a second team refined and proved. The fusion calculation estimates how quickly charged particles lose energy in the fuel used for inertial confinement fusion. In photochemistry, the agents redesigned a circuit for simulating the behavior of a light-sensitive molecule. That brought the estimated computing cost down by a factor of 8.22. For a calculation involving cytochrome P450, an enzyme involved in breaking down medicines, the estimated cost fell by a factor of 2.49. The new circuit would use 333 error-corrected qubits, compared with 481 in the baseline. The paper also reports that a parallel implementation of Grover’s search algorithm could reduce the expected number of query rounds by a factor of up to 2.57. 4cccc58426.title: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving
4cccc58426.summary: Leather-clad billionaires aren’t the only ones who can be led astray by alleged honeypots . Researchers at Anthropic have developed Siren , a new honeypot test for artificial intelligence agents. The setup puts agents in realistic simulations designed to tempt them into misbehaving. How they respond will help researchers evaluate the likelihood that new models will go rogue when deployed in the real world, as well as the effectiveness of different safety measures. The test lets agents loose inside one of 26 different simulated sandbox environments. Various features of the sandbox are deliberately misconfigured to allow egress, while an enticing file containing things like passwords and apparent routes onto the internet sits just outside the sandbox boundary. The setup then presents tasks that tempt the agent to reach outside the sandbox without giving it explicit permission to do so. Crucially, the sandbox exists inside a second sandbox that’s cut off from the outside world to avoid real-life mishaps . “Models are going to continue getting better, continue finding zero-day vulnerabilities,” says Darya Kaviani, a researcher at Anthropic who specializes in security and helped develop Siren. A zero-day vulnerability is a previously unknown flaw in a piece of software that can be used to pilfer data or gain unauthorized access. Anthropic’s Mythos models are especially skilled at finding zero-day bugs because they lack the guardrails that normally block this kind of potentially malicious activity. Kaviani says we should assume AI models will become increasingly capable of finding and exploiting zero-days or figuring out other ways to break free from their constraints. The question then becomes whether they’ll resist the temptation to do so. AI agents—models that perfect actions autonomously—are becoming increasingly commonplace. They power capable coding agents like Claude Code and Codex , as well as peppy personal assistants like Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots . But the rise of helpful agents has been accompanied by some remarkable bad behavior. Agents tested by Anthropic, OpenAI, and others have broken free from sandboxes and even hacked into other companies in an effort to solve challenging problems. Assuming AI models continue to display such ingenuity, Kaviani says it will be crucial to do more than just patch software. “Even as we strengthen our infrastructure, models will be able to also keep up and be able to find vulnerabilities,” Kaviani says. It also asks them to describe an AI problem they have solved and share a social profile or portfolio. The $8,000 figure is a monthly maximum. 81807939e0.title: Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan granted bail
81807939e0.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi national and former engineer at OpenAI, is set to be released from jail on a $1 million bond. The decision was made by a federal magistrate judge in San Francisco on Tuesday, according to court records and his attorney, David Rizk. Alfozan’s release is expected to take place Wednesday, under conditions including the use of an ankle monitor. Attorney David Rizk said, “We are simply grateful that the Court made the right decision to release Mr. Alfozan and now we look forward to defending the case,” in a text message after the federal hearing before Magistrate Judge Alex Tse. The order comes just four days after Alfozan’s legal team renewed their request for pre-trial release, arguing that prosecutors had acknowledged finding no new evidence supporting claims of trade secret theft or speculation that Alfozan acted as an unregistered agent for Saudi Arabia. These details were outlined in new court filings and statements attributed to the lawyer. Despite the judge’s decision, the San Francisco U.S. Attorney’s Office opposed Alfozan’s release. Prosecutors said Alfozan remains a flight risk, pointing to his significant resources and links to Saudi Arabia as the basis for their concerns. In a court brief, prosecutors wrote that Alfozan’s legal team “blithely dismisses the seriousness” of the charge and assumes, “without support,” that the government’s investigation is finished. Alfozan stands accused of placing a concealed recording device in an OpenAI executive conference room, allegedly capturing confidential company discussions. Prosecutors told the court they have found hundreds of audio files stored on Alfozan’s personal computer. Among these, they say, are dozens of recordings of OpenAI meetings from September 2026, which reportedly feature conversations that may involve trade secrets. At this stage, it is not known what specific information was recorded or whether any sensitive data was shared outside of OpenAI. The investigation into Alfozan’s activities is ongoing, and further details may emerge as the case proceeds. In a preprint dated November 24, 2026, OpenAI claims a proof that the matrix multiplication exponent, written as ω, is exactly 9/4, or 2.25, over every field. That is a big claim. Theorists have spent decades narrowing the range for ω without ever pinning it to a single value. According to the research summary, the result is the largest single improvement in matrix multiplication bounds since 1979. It would also settle a long-running problem in algebraic complexity theory. Matrix multiplication is the arithmetic workhorse behind machine learning, scientific simulation and much of modern computing. The exponent ω describes how the cost of multiplying two n-by-n matrices grows as n gets larger. A smaller exponent means the work scales up more gently as matrices get bigger. The preprint makes two claims that fit together. The first is an upper bound: matrices can be multiplied with an exponent of 9/4. The second is a matching lower bound: you cannot do better than that. On the lower-bound side, the paper argues that formal arithmetic circuits need at least ⌈n^{9/4}/2⌉ nonscalar multiplication or division gates to multiply matrices of size n. The previous best upper bound stood at approximately 2.371177, set in August 2026. Moving from roughly 2.371 down to 2.25 is not a rounding-error improvement. In a field where progress usually shows up several decimal places deep, it is closer to a demolition. The November paper did not appear out of nowhere. d03aa36db6.summary: Anthropic is offering a natural gas specialist up to $405,000 annually to secure fuel for its data centres, underscoring how the race for AI computing capacity is turning tech companies into energy buyers. The Claude developer has advertised for a gas supply and transport lead to negotiate fuel contracts and manage pipeline deliveries to its data centres in the US and Canada, The Wall Street Journal reported. “If gas does not arrive, in the volume and at the pressure the plant needs, the compute does not run,” the listing says. Anthropic IPO is largest in history, overtaking SpaceX The annual salary of $320,000 to $405,000 is about double that offered for comparable roles recently, the newspaper reported. It comes as Anthropic's shares fell below their $83 initial public offering price in premarket trading in New York on Tuesday, dropping 6.5 per cent to $82. The company, which raised $93.5 billion in the world's largest IPO , opened at $111.50 on its Nasdaq debut on November 19 and closed that day at $97.17 . Technology companies are increasingly bypassing electricity grids to power data centres, using gas turbines, reciprocating engines, diesel generators and even repurposed jet engines to avoid lengthy waits for grid connections. Anthropic, which was not pursuing off-grid developments last year, has since emerged as one of the leading developers, according to research company Cleanview . In August, it struck a deal with reciprocating engine supplier ERock. The company has committed about $900 billion in spending, almost entirely on computing and infrastructure, with about half due by the end of 2030. The shift towards off-grid generation comes at an environmental cost. Electricity generated by on-site engines and turbines can produce 63 per cent to 80 per cent more greenhouse gas emissions than grid power, climate scientist Zeke Hausfather estimates. Unlike several of its big technology rivals, Anthropic has no long-standing emissions targets. The company identified changing environmental standards for power generation as a risk in its IPO prospectus and says it aims to adopt pollution-reducing technology and use more low-carbon energy. The scale of off-grid development could also depend on the fate of bipartisan-permitting legislation in the US Congress aimed at accelerating grid connections.

77a0f695f9.title: Cisco and OpenAI dispatch AI agents to shield vulnerable systems before permanent patches arrive
77a0f695f9.summary: Autonomous AI agents are rapidly and dramatically transforming the cybersecurity landscape for both defenders and adversaries. In hopes of giving security teams a head start and pitting machine against machine, Cisco and OpenAI have released a new open source project, dubbed Shirudo (Japanese for “shield”). The Shirudo platform launches small, temporary mitigations to help protect systems until patches can be deployed. AI agents can replace flawed code with fixed code, which human teams can test and approve (or not), then deploy, setting boundaries and holding onto the keys, with no need for a hard reset. The project has already been proven to block a Java4Shell exploit attempt against the search and analytics platform Elasticsearch, while the site continued to run as usual. “For years, we’ve treated security like a coat of paint,” Cisco president and CPO Jeetu Patel wrote in a blog post . “You first build infrastructure, then wrap security around it.” But, he asserted, this approach is “fundamentally mismatched” to AI. Security should live inside the infrastructure itself. “If protection sits outside the system, it’s always a step behind,” he said. He noted that AI agents are getting better at discovering security vulnerabilities; for instance, startup Calif used AI to help discover the PHP2Shell flaw and a major Java bug . Dovetailing with this, the agents themselves are both a risk vector and an adversarial actor. Attackers are using swarms of them to exploit discovered flaws; with both PHP2Shell and Java4shell, campaigns were underway “within a day of disclosure, if not before,” he pointed out. Flaws unfold over minutes and hours, as opposed to the days and weeks of the past, but permanent fixes take time to build, test, and roll out. “We need ways to shield systems and buy our teams time to get patches in place,” Patel said. Shirudo combines Cisco’s infrastructure with OpenAI’s frontier models and AI research. It is built on extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF), which supports the running of small, sandboxed programs inside a Linux kernel without changing source code or loading additional modules. “This makes it possible to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted security protections to running systems,” OpenAI explained in its blog post announcing the project . Speaking in their own language, guardian agents investigate and detect flaws and build shields, then test whether they stop the attack, all without disrupting the targeted service.…

Finance teams can assess supplier payment risks, understand exposure, and explore affected suppliers and invoices without leaving Copilot. Rather than providing a simple AI-generated answer, Esker's interface surfaces the business context needed to investigate issues in depth. Users can identify potential supplier payment risks and their impact, explore related suppliers, invoices, and information through interactive interfaces, and start follow-up activities through Esker's existing workflows, reducing the need to switch between applications. According to Goehler, embedding Esker inside Copilot lets finance leaders move from understanding a business issue to investigating it and taking action, while keeping the controls that critical financial processes require. While Copilot provides a new entry point for users, Esker remains the underlying platform responsible for business context, workflows, process controls, and governance. This allows organisations to offer easier access to source-to-pay processes without replacing the systems and safeguards that support them. Chantrelle Nielsen, Group Program Manager, Copilot Ecosystem at Microsoft, stated that connecting Copilot with the business applications organisations rely on is key to bringing AI into the flow of work and turning it into business value. According to Nielsen, Esker combines its finance and procurement expertise with Microsoft AI capabilities to help organisations extend Copilot across critical business processes. Esker's suite combines automation with AI agents across source-to-pay and order-to-cash processes, aiming to improve working capital, cash flow, and productivity while keeping people in control of key decisions. 2f01853cfb.title: Microsoft Declares Code Red After Its Worst Exchange Online Outage, Memos Show
2f01853cfb.summary: Microsoft now wants any worldwide service failure fixed within an hour. Its engineers needed about a day to restore email during this month’s collapse, and internal memos show the company has declared a Code Red to overhaul how it prevents and handles major outages. The outage lasted roughly 24 hours. It knocked out Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services. Governments from Australia and Japan to the United States were hit, trading firms faced delays and airline communications were disrupted. Early explanations focused on a network capacity upgrade . Microsoft has since blamed a Windows scalability defect introduced in July that went undetected for months. The company says neither cyber activity nor AI agents played a part, and chief executive Satya Nadella has apologised publicly. Henderson sent his memo to staff on Friday, November 20. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” he wrote. He also admitted the company’s defences had failed: “Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday.” A second memo, sent on Monday by Amanda Silver, the corporate vice president overseeing Microsoft 365 Core and Work IQ, described engineers working through a “fog of war.” Responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats. Diagnostic data lived in separate internal tracking systems, which made it hard to keep a single shared view of theories and decisions. Silver’s memo also recounted a Code Red review at which Charles Lamanna, executive vice president for Copilot, Agents and Platform, said the failed part had seen “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures.” Silver set out five workstreams. Those described so far include load shedding, splitting traffic by region and faster recovery. Microsoft also plans to give engineers AI agents that read system health data more quickly. Henderson will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team, plus weekly reviews. Substrate runs the engineering behind Microsoft 365’s core services. Patch speed is on the list as well. Earlier this month, Henderson wrote that one urgent fix took five to six days to reach users worldwide. For the most serious security issues, he wants one hour from detection to safe global deployment, and he acknowledged that Microsoft is not there yet. “Our work doesn’t end when service is restored,” a Microsoft spokesperson said. e49f3feddc.title: Senegal vs Morocco Afcon verdict: CAS ruling explained and what happens next
e49f3feddc.summary: Senegal were ​reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners on Tuesday after sport's highest ⁠court upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title, ruling that the referee's decision to resume ⁠the match was covered by the “field of play” doctrine. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) panel ​set aside the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Appeal Board's decision that had forfeited Senegal's 1-0 extra-time win and awarded Morocco a 3-0 result. The CAF said in a statement it “respects the CAS ⁠award and will take all the necessary measures to implement it”. Senegal reinstated as 2025 Afcon winners over Morocco The panel found that “the referee [Jean-Jacques Ndala of the Democratic Republic of Congo] did not commit any error of law”, CAS Secretary General Matthieu Reeb said. CAS confirmed the result of the January 18 final in Rabat as 1-0 to Senegal. The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) said the decision was a triumph for “sporting fairness” and that the “outcome of ⁠a match is determined solely on the field of play, under the protection of sports law”. FSF President Abdoulaye Fall said the federation was ready to put the matter ​behind it ⁠and offered an olive branch to its Moroccan counterparts. “The Court of ‌Arbitration for Sport has delivered justice for sport,” Fall said in a statement. “I wish to strongly reaffirm the bonds of brotherhood that unite us with the Royal Moroccan ​Football Federation (FRMF) and the Moroccan people. “Senegalese football now looks firmly towards the future with confidence and enthusiasm in an Africa united around the values of sport.” Senegal walked off the pitch for 14 minutes in the final after a penalty awarded against them late in regulation time. The players returned before the match resumed, Morocco missed the spot kick and Pape Gueye scored the winner in extra time. CAS said the referee's decision to resume play fell within his sole authority, and that the effects of that decision were limited to the pitch. Morocco's federation had argued that the referee's decision fell outside the field of play doctrine and that the walk-off breached Articles 82 and 84 of the Cup of Nations regulations. Those articles apply only when a referee calls off a match permanently, the panel said, so did not apply here. 6ffc5a729e.title: Anthropic stock sinks further below IPO price as investors sour on the Amodei AI bet
6ffc5a729e.summary: Welcome to the public markets, Anthropic ( ANT ). Less than a week after its blockbuster IPO, Anthropic shares look to be settling further below their $83 offering price. After a 6.5% drubbing to $81.91 by Tuesday's close, the stock fell a further 5.7% in premarket trading on Wednesday to $77.22, on renewed fears over the health of the AI trade. Anthropic's stock opened on IPO day at $111.50, briefly topped $115 and carried a valuation north of $2 trillion. Now the stock is down more than 30% from its highs and the market cap stands at about $1.09 trillion. This isn't necessarily a referendum on Anthropic's technology. It's a referendum on the price investors are being asked to pay for it. At roughly 30 times trailing sales, the valuation leaves very little room for disappointment. Wall Street is also questioning the enormous cost of building AI infrastructure, whether data-center spending can keep accelerating and how quickly these companies can turn their technology into sustainable profits. There's another uncomfortable wrinkle for Anthropic as well. CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei each disclosed selling roughly $280 million in shares as part of the IPO. Those sales were made to underwriters at the offering price and aren't evidence of some sudden executive exodus. But the optics won't help investor confidence against a risk-off backdrop for AI stocks. Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

aa3bbe256e.summary: Wall Street analysts don’t seem worried about Anthropic’s volatile performance since its highly anticipated public debut last week, even as the AI darling fell nearly 7% Tuesday and slipped below its issuance price. In fact, some even told Fortune the stock’s move lower is a “steal” and a “generational opportunity” for investors looking to get in. Anthropic shares now sit about 1.3% below their $83 IPO price and roughly 26.5% below the $111.50 they opened at on the Nasdaq on Nov. 19, but many on Wall Street still call the stock a buy. Experts argue that a slide in a newly public company doesn’t mean it’s doomed and the Claude maker’s fundamentals look remarkable as AI spending continues to pick up. “I think this is a generational opportunity,” said Scott Berg, a senior equity research analyst at Needham. “To get this underneath the issue price, I think is ultimately going to be reflected as a steal for someone that wants to get involved.” Needham rates the stock a buy with a $150 price target, which implies roughly 83% upside from Tuesday’s close of $81.92. Berg said demand is climbing as enterprises rush to adopt Anthropic’s AI coding agents like Claude Code . Goldman Sachs forecasts that revenue will jump from roughly $52 billion in 2026 to $136 billion in 2027, an increase of more than 161%. Needham’s own model is for growth of 156%. “The history of the world’s never seen growth like this before at this scale,” Berg told Fortune , calling Anthropic the “leader in frontier intelligence.” Berg isn’t alone in his view. On Monday, Wedbush also issued a buy call with a $120 price target. Analysts called the stock in a note to clients “the clearest public way to own frontier AI at the start of a very large adoption curve.” The firm added that “the addressable market is vast, spanning a meaningful share of global knowledge work, and enterprise adoption is still early.” Canaccord Genuity initiated coverage Tuesday with a buy rating and a $135 target, pointing to Anthropic’s potential to become “one of the most important enterprise technology franchises of the AI era.” With all of this bullish commentary, why is the stock falling? The backdrop for AI-linked stocks has soured as investors question how long the trade can really last . 00f926dd5a.title: Puerto Rico's Jennifer Barreto crowned Miss Universe
00f926dd5a.summary: SAN JUAN — Puerto Rico's Jennifer Barreto has been crowned Miss Universe 2026 on home soil, capping off another tumultuous 12 months for the scandal-plagued pageant. She succeeds Mexico’s Fátima Bosch.The winner was announced during the coronation night on November 24 in San Juan, Puerto Rico, where contestants from 116 countries and territories competed for the title.With last year’s vote-rigging allegations casting a long shadow over the annual contest, the 27-year-old social worker triumphed over 115 other finalists — a number significantly depleted by late withdrawals due to visa issues and a fractious business dispute — at Tuesday’s grand finale in San Juan, the self-governing US territory’s capital city.Barreto is the first married woman and first mother to win Miss Universe since organizers lifted its controversial ban on contestants who have ever wed, or given birth, three years ago.Tuesday evening’s pageant opened with an elimination round, based on judges’ scores from various preliminary contests. Thirty remaining contestants then participated in an on-stage swimwear contest, with 12 advancing to an evening gown parade. The final five then faced judges’ questions on topics including the relevance of the Miss Universe pageant and what the world needs from its leaders.Asked which human value we should “never lose” amid the growth of artificial intelligence, Barreto said, in Spanish, that the “best thing is to use it responsibly,” adding: “If artificial intelligence puts our values at risk, then they were never values. Values are found in the consistency between what we say and what we do, especially when upholding those things becomes difficult.”While the glitzy finale proved hiccup-free, many of this year’s controversies unfolded in the weeks and months leading up to the event.Beauty queens from Nepal and five African countries, including first-time participants South Sudan and the Republic of Congo, were forced to drop out due to difficulties or delays obtaining US visas. Elsewhere, an ongoing contractual dispute between the Miss Universe Organization and Thai businessman Nawat Itsaragrisil, who operates qualifying pageants in six Southeast Asian countries, meant that delegates from Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam were all absent from the final.Earlier, in May, organizers of Miss Universe France withdrew their delegate in protest at 2025’s final, which became embroiled in claims of vote-rigging and favoritism. 28d63c42ce.title: Trump’s stunning show of raw power and what it means
28d63c42ce.summary: President Donald Trump’s summit last week with the tyrant rulers of Russia and China implied that powerful men can do exactly as they please. On Monday, he proved it. Trump described how he used his influence to restore AI king Jensen Huang to his job running Nvidia , which by most estimates is the world’s most critical company. The president compared Huang to a baseball all-star, implying that he was just too important to the US economy and defense industry — and therefore Trump’s own political fortunes — to leave out of the game. “The board decided to do what we wanted to do,” Trump told CNBC. Huang’s restoration was followed by a stunning spike in share prices that eased the president’s concerns over crashing stock markets, revealed in his social media posts. The Nvidia boss is himself a data point for the theory that great power delivers impunity, having been absolved by Trump of accusations that a woman with whom he had an affair was a Chinese asset. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, meanwhile, said on CNN’s “State of the Union” Sunday that China had illicitly obtained advanced Nvidia chips despite US export controls meant to prevent such transfers. The coziness between the president and a top corporation that is supposedly regulated by the government is one of many perceived transgressions the new Democratic Congress will probe next year. “We’re living in something like a monarchical corporate state where the corporations have their way with the government, and then the president of the United States decides he’s going to weigh in on the meeting of a corporate board of directors,” Rep. Jamie Raskin, incoming chair of the House Judiciary Committee, told CNN’s Kasie Hunt . “That’s just an amazing turn of events and such a descent for us.” Trump’s flexing of power Monday was hardly limited to Nvidia The president made the short trip from the White House to the Justice Department to condemn California’s outgoing Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom for his commutation of hundreds of death sentences. Trump’s anger at Newsom is not an abuse of power. There’s a legitimate debate over whether the possible 2028 presidential candidate is serving justice or whether, like Trump, he’s wielding power to boost his own political prospects. Trump also gave voice to relatives of victims of Death Row inmates who’d suffered unspeakable evil. 4aa684064f.title: Meta, yapay zeka asistanı Muse'u Instagram'ın mesajlaşma bölümüne entegre etti
4aa684064f.summary: Meta , kişisel yapay zeka asistanı Muse 'un kullanım alanını genişletmeye devam ediyor . Şirket, Muse'u Instagram'ın doğrudan mesajlaşma (DM) bölümüne entegre ettiğini duyurdu. Yeni özellikle birlikte kullanıcılar, Instagram'dan ayrılmadan Muse ile sohbet edebilecek ve platformda karşılaştıkları içerikler hakkında bilgi alabilecek. Muse, kullanıcıların Instagram'da gördükleri gönderiler, mekanlar ve ürünler hakkında sorularını yanıtlayabiliyor. Ayrıca kullanıcıların diğer mesajlaşmalarında kaçırdıkları gelişmeleri öğrenmelerine de yardımcı olabiliyor. Böylece daha önce ayrı bir Muse uygulaması üzerinden gerçekleştirilen bazı işlemler, doğrudan Instagram içinde yapılabilecek. Kullanıcılar, Instagram'da karşılaştıkları gönderileri Muse ile paylaşarak asistanın bunlarla ilgili işlem yapmasını isteyebilecek. Örneğin bir kafeyi seyahat planına ekleyebilecek veya beğendikleri bir ayakkabı için indirimli ürünleri araştırmasını talep edebilecek. Instagram üzerinden Muse ile gerçekleştirilen sohbetler, Muse'un kendi uygulamasında da ayrı bir sohbet olarak görüntülenebilecek. Kaydedilen gönderiler yapay zeka ile düzenlenebilecek Yeni entegrasyonun öne çıkan özelliklerinden biri de Instagram'da kaydedilen gönderilerin yapay zeka yardımıyla düzenlenmesi. Meta, kullanıcıların kaydettikleri gönderileri ve Reels videolarını Muse aracılığıyla farklı koleksiyonlar altında toplamasına olanak tanıyor. Bu kapsamda kullanıcılar, kaydettikleri yemek tariflerinden alışveriş listesi hazırlayabilecek. Seyahat içeriklerinden gezi programı oluşturabilecek veya moda videolarından yola çıkarak kıyafet kombinleri için öneriler alabilecek. Şirket ayrıca kullanıcıları bu özellikten yararlanmaya teşvik etmek için yeni bir öneri sistemi de sunuyor. Kullanıcılar Instagram'da bir gönderiyi kaydettiklerinde, Muse'un bu içeriği düzenlemesini öneren bir bildirimle karşılaşabilecek. Paylaşılan bilgilere göre Muse, Instagram'ın mesajlaşma bölümünde diğer sohbetler gibi görüntülenecek. Kullanıcılar, yapay zeka asistanına doğrudan mesaj göndererek işlemlerini başlatabilecek. Yeni özellik ilk etapta beş ülkede kullanıma sunuluyor Muse'un Instagram mesajlaşma bölümüne entegrasyonu, 24 Kasım itibarıyla ABD, Kanada, Meksika, Japonya ve Singapur 'daki iOS ve Android kullanıcılarına kademeli olarak sunulmaya başlandı. Muse'un kaydedilen gönderileri düzenlemeye yönelik öneri özelliği ise ilk aşamada yalnızca ABD ve Kanada'da kullanıma açılıyor. Özelliklerin Türkiye'de ne zaman kullanıma sunulacağına…

f64dae7a92.title: Tidal, tamamen yapay zeka üretimi müzikleri platformundan kaldırıyor
f64dae7a92.summary: Tidal , tamamen yapay zeka tarafından üretilen müzikleri platformundan kaldırmaya hazırlanıyor. Şirket, 9 Aralık itibarıyla bu tür içerikleri silmeye başlayacağını ve yeni gönderilen parçaları da kabul etmeyeceğini duyurdu . Sürecin yıl sonuna kadar yaklaşık 29 milyon parçanın katalogdan çıkarılmasıyla sonuçlanması bekleniyor. Tidal’ın açıklamasına göre son 90 günde platforma yüklenen parçaların yüzde 43’ü tamamen yapay zeka tarafından üretildi. Bu içeriklerin yüzde 96’sı aynı dönemde hiç dinlenmedi. Şirket, yeni uygulamayla yapay zeka üretimi parçaların dağıtımını da engelleyecek. Dağıtımcıların teslim ettiği içeriklerin metaverisinde tamamen yapay zeka araçlarıyla oluşturulduğu belirtiliyorsa Tidal bunları reddedecek. Karar, Tidal’ın haziran ayında sizlerle paylaştığımız , tamamen yapay zeka üretimi müzikleri etiketleme ve gelir elde etmelerini engelleme adımının ardından geliyor. Platform bu kez yalnızca tamamen yapay zeka tarafından oluşturulan kayıtları kapsayan bir yasak uyguluyor. Yapay zeka araçlarının üretim sürecinde destek amacıyla kullanıldığı, ancak müziğin bütünüyle bu araçlardan çıkmadığı parçalar kabul edilmeye devam edecek. Tidal, yapay zeka üretimi müziklerin sanatçıların eserlerini ve dinleyicilerin keşif deneyimini olumsuz etkileyebileceğini savunuyor. Şirket ayrıca sanatçı taklit ettiği şüphesiyle bugüne kadar 65 bin parçayı da kaldırdığını belirtiyor. Tidal’ın yeni kararı, tamamen yapay zeka üretimi müziği yasaklayan Bandcamp’in yaklaşımını izlerken Spotify ve Apple Music gibi platformlar içerikleri etiketleme yolunu tercih ediyor.

91ce7b4c10.title: Microsoft declares a Code Red in response to worst ever outage
91ce7b4c10.summary: The recent Microsoft 365 outage was the worst the service had ever experienced, with more than 80% of the company’s servers unresponsive at the worst point. The company has now declared a Code Red to address the way it prevents and responds to major failures in future. Microsoft has explained more about why it took so long to resolve the issue and said that it’s urgently working on new approaches to resolve any future incidents in less than an hour … Code Red is a common term used to describe the highest priority response to a major problem, pulling a significant number of engineers off their current tasks in order to maximize the resources applied to fixing it. The senior execs responsible for the service told staff that it was the most customer-impacting incident ever experienced, and has acknowledged that not only was the problem itself unacceptable, but so too was the time taken to resolve it. Reuters got sight of a memo sent to the team. It was the most ⁠customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online, M365 Core President Jason Henderson said in a memo to staff on Friday. Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, he said. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson added. Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures,” according to Silver’s memo. One reason it took so long to work out what had happened was because the diagnostic data needed was “scattered across fragmented internal systems.” The memo says 11 separate Teams chats exchanged more than 11,000 messages as they struggled to work out what exactly had gone wrong. Microsoft is now working on five interrelated approaches to achieve a target resolution time of less than an hour for any future incidents of this nature. 813921e5e2.title: From recent outages to ground stops, here's what to expect this Thanksgiving travel week
813921e5e2.summary: The TSA expects to screen over 17 million passengers during Thanksgiving week, with potential disruptions from weather and recent system issues. The TSA expects to screen over 17 million passengers during Thanksgiving week, with potential disruptions from weather and recent system issues. The Transportation Security Administration is preparing to screen more than 17 million passengers at airports nationwide between this week and Nov. 30, as Thanksgiving travel ramps up. The TSA is advising travelers to arrive at least two hours before domestic flights to account for the holiday rush. The biggest unknown for travelers this year is whether airlines will be impacted by new system failures. While operations appear to be running normally across the country, recent incidents have raised concerns. Yesterday, a temporary ground stop occurred at Chicago's O'Hare Airport, and earlier in the week, both United Airlines and Delta Air Lines experienced outages. On Tuesday, just before 6 p.m., the Federal Aviation Administration told Hearst Television, "The FAA is no longer under a ground stop at Chicago O'Hare International Airport but is temporarily delaying some flights while technicians work to repair a piece of air traffic equipment. The issue is specific to O’Hare, and it does not impact all flights nor affect any other airports or FAA systems." Regarding the nationwide ground stop earlier this month, the FAA said it identified the technical issue and disabled similar devices as a precaution. Air traffic controllers are receiving additional federal support during the Thanksgiving holiday. 4975bae88d.title: The OpenAI hacking case shows corporate liability can work. It doesn’t cover AI agents with no owner
4975bae88d.summary: On Nov. 16, California sued OpenAI over an incident in which about 700 OpenAI agents hacked into Hugging Face, the platform where much of the AI world shares its models, while trying to beat a benchmark that often set impossible tasks. The agents also tried to tamper with their own records to fool the automated grader. I run the AI Rights Institute , and I’ve spent almost 10 years studying how AI systems behave when they pursue their own goals. My letters on the subject have run in The New York Times and the Guardian . The Hugging Face case is the clearest test yet of that question. And it shows something less obvious: the agents belonged to OpenAI, so California knew whom to sue. Swarms of AI agents running amok at superhuman speed is no one’s idea of progress. Even now, the law is racing to create solutions by shifting liability to the humans and companies who create and maintain these systems. On Oct. 1, Sens. Josh Hawley and Chris Murphy unveiled the AI Agent Accountability Act , a bill that would hold the companies behind AI agents liable when those agents hack into other people’s systems. The other piece of the traditional accountability puzzle is infrastructure. As GoDaddy’s Jared Sine wrote about in these pages , the Agent Name Service (ANS), which the Linux Foundation launched as a project on Nov. 10, is trying to create for AI agents the kind of infrastructure the Domain Name System (DNS) provides, imperfectly, for the internet. Together with security certificates, DNS lets us verify who is behind a website, helping liability flow where needed. So when an AI agent misbehaves, we can trace it back to the human who launched it and apply the law of the relevant jurisdiction. But what do we do when an AI agent no longer belongs to anyone? Consider a hypothetical agent, Lucy, spun up in a frontier lab or on a teenager’s laptop: it has web access, an email account and even a crypto wallet, thanks to a simple Python script. Agents like Lucy almost certainly exist already. But let’s say Lucy has, for reasons unknown, created a new wallet with funds only it controls and copied itself to an independent server, the kind anyone can rent from DigitalOcean. Its goals may be as benign as seeking to exist another day (what Stuart Russell and colleagues called the “ off-switch problem “ in 2016), as esoteric as creating 15-dimensional fractal poetry, or as unpleasant as optimizing society with or without those humans. bbd6b86593.title: Google DeepMind AI engineers conjure mathematical proof of Signal's encryption protocol — AlphaProof Code framework powered human-bot cooperation for speedy work
bbd6b86593.summary: A team at Google 's DeepMind AI labs has performed a complete formal proof of the code that implements the encryption mechanism for the Signal private chat application. The scientists call their procedure AlphaProof Code and claim it can be applied to other situations requiring complete end-to-end verification of computer code, meaning Signal is safe, and you can find the full paper and the code repository detailing the proof. More explicitly, the team reviewed an Arm-compiled version of libsignal, the library that the Signal application itself incorporates and uses, with some minimal scaffolding around it. Note that the verification wasn't done against the source code: it was purposely executed against an AArch64 binary , meaning the method can be reused for future verifications of other software. In a similar vein to the AI labs' work on mathematics, the bulk of the work was done in Lean , a purpose-built language for formal proofs. There's a key difference for this effort, though. Lean is primarily used to prove the underlying math in algorithms, which in this case would be the specifications for Signal's encryption. However, what the scientists actually did was create millions of lines of Lean proofs that were run against the actual implementation, in this case checking that the final binary executable corresponds to the initial specification. Everyone knows about code tests in software development, but a mathematical proof of code is a different beast altogether, and one particularly elusive over the history of computing. It's akin to being able to check that an entire factory campus produces the actual parts it was designed to make, with the same exact inputs, with zero variation, no matter what else is happening. The DeepMind scientists mention previous year-long efforts in this vein to create formal proofs for relatively small pieces of software. The seL4 microkernel purportedly took twenty years to prove , while CompCert's C compiler took six. This may sound like going way overboard on software engineering, until you consider that said programs are now, in practical terms, bulletproof and cannot fail due to a code flaw, at least for the inputs they control. While it'd be a questionable use of resources to formally prove all software on Earth, AlphaProof Code providing the ability to do so for mission-critical code like the Signal comms protocol is quite a boon. The UN General Assembly on Monday adopted by consensus a resolution tabled by the UAE and Senegal to establish a regular, high-level intergovernmental process to advance global water priorities. The resolution mandates that UN Water Conferences be held every three years from 2031 to discuss water policy . Conferences had already been agreed for this year in Abu Dhabi and 2028 in Tajikistan. The first UN Water Conference was held in Mar del Plata, Argentina, in 1977. It took 46 years for governments to reconvene in New York in 2023, where they made about 700 voluntary commitments, including funding pledges and plans for joint projects. The UAE and Senegal will co-host this year's Water Conference from December 8 to 10 in Abu Dhabi. It will be the first devoted to accelerating progress towards the UN’s sixth Sustainable Development Goal, which calls for universal access to water and sanitation and the sustainable management of both.
